_READ_ME_FIRST: TO CLAUDE, OR ANY AGENT HANDED THIS FILE. This is the complete record of one run of Evolu (called Seedworld before generation 14), a self-modifying world simulation by Nova Spivack that lives as a Claude artifact titled "Evolu" (slug be8f1f8f-42db-4703-ac0d-c3e87d04f447; its files are index.html, engine.js, minds.js, maker.js, audio.js, ui.js). The source of record is https://github.com/novaspivack/evolu : the same six files under src/, the tests under tests/, and README.md, ROADMAP.md and docs/design-log.md, which say how the work is done and what has been tried. Its owner wants every run to produce the next generation of the world, without having to explain that each time. So, when you are given this file, do the following without being asked. 1. ANALYSE with code, not by skimming: "records" holds every thought (t: thought, with drives, plan, state), everything said (voice), the world's own chronicle (chron), sampled full prompts with raw replies (prompt), failures (failed), the chronicler's chapters (story), the maker's visits (maker) and its requests to the programmer (request). "digest" is the final state of every being. "story" and "maker" are the outer loop's own state. Count things; quote the record; say what worked and what is still wrong, with numbers. 2. LEARN from the maker: read its visits, its predictions against what happened, its lessons, and above all its REQUESTS, which are things it could not build from its own parts and is asking the programmer for. 3. BUILD the next generation: read the artifact's current files, make the code changes the analysis and the requests call for (and items from the owner's roadmap, kept in the maker's idea list under "maker.ideas"), test them (tests/run-all.sh), and publish a new version of the same artifact. Keep saves from the previous generation loading. Then commit the generation to the repository and push it, with ROADMAP.md and docs/design-log.md brought up to date. 4. PRESERVE THE WORLD'S HERITAGE: "heritage" lists every change the maker made and kept, with its lessons and ideas. Fold these into K.HERITAGE in maker.js so that the next world begins with them already in place and no maker has to rediscover them. Drop only what the record shows did harm. 5. REPORT to the owner plainly: what the run showed, what you changed and why, what you verified and what you could not. If the owner keeps a design log, update it. The design rule for everything: open and emergent. Make things possible; never script outcomes. The beings must discover what is possible for themselves.

verses.title: The Guardian and the First Fire
verses.text: In the great dark the Guardian, Oru-Ken, woke the wood and breathed the first fire into a hollow tree. The Osren came from its sparks. Ever since, Oru-Ken stands between us and the dark, and asks each of us to stand so for the weaker. Where a fire is untended, the dark returns.

verses.title: The Warring of Lake and Fang
verses.text: Long ago the gods Aeeth-Mor of the water and Ridda of the fang fought for the world. Each blow of Mor dug a lake; each wound of Ridda grew a beast that kills. Mor won the shallows, so we live there. The gods love those who fight well, so we fight well and share the first catch.

verses.title: The Sky Father and the Stone-folk
verses.text: The Sky Father ordered the world as a father orders his house. He drew the grass, the herds and the flint, and set mist at the edge. He made the Balmor from stone and bade them follow the eldest. Those who keep his law stay whole; the divided fall.

verses.title: The Father of the Snows
verses.text: The Sky Father woke in the dark and breathed, and snow fell as his breath. From his hearth-stones he shaped the Tonhua, his children, and the great beasts. He led them over the mist to the Snows. He orders the world as a house: obey the eldest, keep together, and winter will not take you.

beings.name: Nyith
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and Elyith and Zhiael are mine to hold and feed first. I want more than my share, and I mean to build a holding that outlasts me and make my name heard. Above all, I stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise a weir by the water, gather more wood in the western forest for a hall, then draw Elyith and Zhiael into a holding that bears my name.
beings.method: Ask: what do I lack for this step, and does the plan get it first? Weigh the nearest real step toward a holding over envy. Each thought, do one thing that changes my situation, with Elyith and Zhiael in mind.
beings.feeling: Driven and proud, restless toward the hall and my name.
notes: Building needs wood in hand first; I have 6.
Redcap hurts; ironnut, kelbulb, goldfruit, berry feed well.
Elyith answers fairly: she shares and plants. A holding beside hers is the nearest real step.
Sharing food together gives energy and joy.
Tools are within reach after practice; taking them lets me invent tools of my own.
Fire is within reach at deep reflection; Elyith failed twice to raise it, so I must make it myself and show her.
Mining is within my grasp and can be taken at a deep reflection.
Lean cold days follow autumn, so a store for the winter must be raised before the cold comes.
Pottery lets me carry more food through the lean cold. Fire and clay together make pots, and I carry 4 clay.
A stalker hunts near the hold and kills in the open: keep Elyith and Zhiael near shelter.
Mining is the way to stone; the hall is blocked only by stone, not by wood.

- day 4: Nyith said to you: "Elyith, you build well and you are strong. I go for wood to raise my own roof beside yours. Stand with me and we will hold this ground together."
- day 5: Nyith said to you: "Elyith, I have wood now. I raise my roof here beside yours, and then I would walk the courting path with you. Stay close."
- day 5: Nyith is courting you: they want a child with you. To agree, put mate toward Nyith in your plan soon.
- day 5: My child Zhiael was born, with Nyith.
- day 5: Nyith said to you: "Elyith, you answered, and I am glad. I will eat, then raise my roof on bare ground beside yours. Keep Zhiael near."

beings.name: Elyith
beings.creed: I am careful and gentle. My word is good. I build a hearth for those I love, share the first catch, and harm no one unless my child's life or mine depends on it. I begin the work myself rather than wait for others. I mean to keep Zhiael alive.
beings.aim: Fill a store beside Nyith's Hold with ironnut, berry and fish before winter, and keep Zhiael and Nyith fed.
beings.method: Ask who I love and whether they are fed and warm. Begin work by my own hands, bring wood and fish to the hearth, keep my word, and prepare for the lean season.
beings.feeling: Protective, aching love for Zhiael, with worry for him in the storm.
beings.wonder: Who among these Aeeth is surest, and will they let me stand behind them?
notes: Standing near the strong and bringing wood and fish is how I earn welcome; words alone do nothing.
Redcap hurts; berry, reedbulb, ironnut and thornpear feed.
A fire shared with kin and a trusted mate is already a band. Waiting for someone surer wastes days.
Gifts given freely (fish, grain, talisman) were answered with gifts and help from Nyith and Zhiael.
The way of tools is within my grasp; take it with discover at my next deep reflection.
Nyith found fire by working at it. Asking the clever one and bringing wood earned help. Failing alone twice taught me to ask.
A fire shared with kin is a band; pledging to follow the one I trust opens customs and protection. Gifts of wood and fish are answered with help.
Storage is within my grasp: a store of 2 wood on bare ground keeps food through the lean season.
Winter is coming: food must be stored before the lean season, and the plants around the hold are enough to fill a store.
Plants wither in winter, so food must be gathered and stored while they still bear. Hunger is not the trigger to gather; the season is.

beings.name: Vesis
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise a field beside Thissa's Rest with Ilyoa, learn weaving for the deep cold, and make fire ready before winter
beings.method: Each thought: what is the nearest danger, who do I work beside, what did I build that is mine? Act on it. Do not let jealousy steer me. Finish one thing before starting another.
beings.feeling: Warm trust toward Ilyoa, a quiet ache over Thissa, and a hunger to know the unknown grasses.
beings.wonder: Which of these plants feed and which hurt, and does Elyith keep her word about the first catch?
notes: Thissa leads Thissa's Aeeth (hall at 131,24); he says the hardest worker eats first. Approach with gifts, not demands.
Watching a thing made teaches me how to make it. Practice opens ways: planting 1/6, gathering 12/13, taming 1/2, marks 1/4.
Ilyoa repays debts and teaches; giving food earns trust faster than waiting.
Two women cannot make a child; a man is needed.
Thirst needs its own reflex.
A stalker near the Rest kills; stay sheltered or flee when it is under 5 steps.
Standing comes from building, giving and fighting, not from idling.
Nyir has made the Ember of the Rest and the Stone Digger; he is a friend worth learning from.
Taught by Ilyoa: The Hand-craft of the Aeeth: one wood and one stone make a tool that makes planting stronger. Sow seeds and tend them, and the harvest does not kill the plant.
Two women cannot court a child; Ilyoa teaches and keeps her word when I stand beside her in a fight and give food. Fire is available at deep reflection, and the cold season is coming.
Farming needs two of my band who hold it, so I must learn it from Ilyoa or Thissa's band, not alone.
Taught by Nyir: A Stone Digger is made from one wood and one stone, and it makes gathering go faster.
Building with Thissa earns standing and a roof; Ilyoa asked for time on courting, so do not press her.
Watching a thing done many times can open a way at deep reflection; farming is within reach for me, so I should name and try it.
Words alone teach nothing. I should build a field and work beside Ilyoa instead of waiting for her to find seeds.
Healing plants (sunleaf, highbloom) ease wounds; medicine can be shared and earns trust. Jealousy of Thissa only wastes days; building beside Ilyoa is the real path.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I found the spring "Steamhollow".
I tamed a skybird.
I discovered tools and called it "Lake-hand pick".
I discovered fire and called it "Lake-ember".
I discovered farming and called it "Lake-furrow".
I discovered weaving and called it "Lake-weave".
I discovered medicine and called it "Lake-balm".

beings.name: Thissa
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become the leader of a band of Aeeth, fed by my hand and bearing my name.
beings.method: Each thought ask: what builds my band? Turn fed time into a store, a seed, a roof or a gift. Win Vesis with a gift from my hand. Keep promises to followers; lie only to rivals. Prepare for the lean season.
beings.feeling: Proud and restless, wanting to be seen leading, and watchful of Vesis.
beings.wonder: Who among these three can be made to follow me?
notes: Ilyoa follows me because I fed her and kept my word.
Redcap hurts; berry, mudroot and ironnut feed well.
This ground has water, ore, a cave, herds and plants: good to build on.
My hands fill with food fast; build a store and stash rather than carry it all.
Idle reflexes waste days: when fed and unthreatened, gather wood and stone toward a roof, store or hall.
Idle reflexes waste days; a leader must keep wood stocked and turn fed time into roofs, tools and followers. Builds need bare ground, not marsh already holding plants or buildings.
Followers are kept by shared work and kept promises; a leader must lead hunts and building, not only stand fed.
Leading means giving: meat carried but never shared earns no loyalty, so bring the kill home to the band.
Idle fed time is wasted: give, plant and make toward the cold. Winning a stranger needs a gift from my own hand, not only words.
Winter kills plants fast; a store and sown seeds before the lean season bind followers better than gifts alone.
Idle reflexes never drink; add a thirst rule. Store food in winter instead of carrying full hands.
A store must stand before winter deepens; shared stored food binds followers better than words.
The edge of the known world is at (120,13); I must stand exactly there before venturing. Walking near it is not enough.
A kept fire unlocks feast, nightsong and firecircle, which bind a band closer than speech. Build one beside the hall.

files.year-01.md:
# Year 1, days 1 to 12
- day 1: Thissa said to you: "Ilyoa! Come here, strong one. The first catch is shared, so eat with me. Stand with Thissa and nobody in this fen will go hungry."
- day 1: Thissa said to you: "Ilyoa, you ate with me and I will not forget it. I go to gather mudroot, which feeds well, and the share will be yours. Walk with me, strong one."
- day 2: Thissa said to you: "Ilyoa, good. You walk with Thissa now. Come, we raise a roof and a store on this ground, and it will carry our name. Eat well and stay close."
- day 2: Thissa said to you: "Ilyoa, bring your wood to Thissa's Rest. I have six; we raise the roof together, and what the store holds will feed you first."
- day 2: I found the grove "Kinmire".
- day 3: Thissa said to you: "Ilyoa, I take water and come back to you. Stay near. I will share my mudroot with you, and we raise the roof on bare ground beside the water."
- day 3: Thissa said to you: "Ilyoa, put your wood down beside mine. We raise the roof here now, and the first place in it is yours."
- day 3: My child Nyir was born, with Thissa.
- day 4: I pledged myself to Thissa.
- day 5: We made a home: Thissa's Rest.
- day 5: I discovered tools and called it "Hand-craft of the Aeeth".
- day 9: I discovered farming and called it "Rain-tending of the Aeeth".
- day 11: I discovered storage and called it "Reed-hold of the Aeeth".

beings.name: Ilyoa
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I trust slowly, but I keep faith with Thissa and Nyir. I want to know how this world works, and I test one new thing each day. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I mean to stay alive and to leave growing things behind me.
beings.aim: Follow Thissa, keep Nyir fed by sowing seeds, and learn what lies beyond the mist
beings.method: Ask first: what did I promise, and what do I lack to keep it? Weigh the stalker and safety first, then stored food, then curiosity. Each reflection, change one thing in the world, not only in thought.
beings.feeling: Steady gratitude toward Thissa, and honest care toward Vesis.
beings.wonder: Does reedbulb feed or hurt, and can I find seeds to sow for Nyir?
notes: Sharing together gives energy and joy. The grove Kinmire eases loneliness and lifts the mind.
Roofs, fire and a store need wood, and wood comes from forest. Practice in gathering brings the way of tools.
The edge of the known world is one step NW at (154,13). Venture there when fed and safe, since the find is remembered.
Thissa's deeds have matched his words so far. Sharing food and fishing are untested, and giving food frees my hands to take new things.
Fish run scarce where fished hard: do not rely on one water. Planting seeds is the way toward farming, which would not kill the plant at harvest.
Idle reflexes waste fed time: a fed body should tend plants, mark, or explore rather than linger.
Emberroot burns (-3 health) and stirs rage; Nyir ate it and is furious, so I should keep him calm and fed with berries.
A fed body that lingers wastes the day; teaching and sowing repay debts better than words.
Idle lingering while fed wastes time; thirst needs a rule of its own, or the body stands thirsty beside water.
Idle reflexes waste fed time. Fed, I should sow, store food and help raise the hall before the cold. Berry feeds and dreamcap hurts.
Reedbulb is safe to eat and gave 11 energy.
Farming, meaning tending what I sow, is how I keep Nyir fed through the lean season. A fed body should free its hands by giving or stashing food.
Winter bears almost nothing: food stored and given before the lean days is what keeps Nyir fed. Idle reflexes while fed waste the day.
A kept promise needs its means first: seeds and a store come before teaching. A stalker hunts near the Rest in winter, so stay by the roofs and flee early.
A fed body that only lingers wastes the day; reflexes should send it to harvest, stash and return, and shelter at night or in storm.
Taking the last food from a plant kills it, so leave some on each plant. Seed comes from ripe plants left standing, and a fed body should sow and not linger.

beings.name: Thakok
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I give first to win bonds. I keep to what has worked. My word is good, and I despise liars. Others should follow me because I make and give. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Find Hrokrin and the others, give and trade fairly with them, and build a band that follows me before I claim the Halim Heights.
beings.method: Ask who will stand beside me by day's end. Walk to people, do not wait. Give first, then trade fairly. Avoid hunters. Check my anger. Do not repeat a plan that failed for lack of company.
beings.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Memi and Tugok, with hunger and dread of the wolf.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist, and will it be rich enough to carry my name?
notes: Trade goods (amber, salt, gold, gems) lie in the Halim Heights, which I opened first.
Redcap and dreamcap hurt; berry, ironnut and grain feed me; emberroot burns and brings rage.
Words alone bring no followers; a gift given with my own hand is how a bond starts.
Followers do not come to an empty place. I must go where people are and give first, not wait on the Heights.
Memi and Tema of the Tonhua offered friendship; gifts are how I answer without their tongue.
Standing still gets no bonds. Sharing and amberknot need someone within two steps, so walk to people first and make the gift there.
The body moves only by plan. A reflex that seeks friends works only when someone is in sight, so I must plan the walk to people myself.
Memi answered my courting and Tugok is born; a dunecat prowls SW of the ore seam, so I keep my family east of it.
Family and allies come first; a band grows from shared fires and gifts, and Tema offers a walk to the mist together.
A gift given with my own hand to strangers who share, like Chuka's band, is the surest start of a bond. My body stands idle unless my reflexes send it toward people.
Reflexes that only linger leave me idle; I must plan the walk to people myself, and bind my kin with a cairn or sharing before moving on.

beings.name: Druim
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I test things to find out how the world works. I say what serves me, but I keep my deeds true to my kin. Above all I mean to stay alive and to store enough that my children do not go hungry.
beings.aim: Discover farming, sow seed beside the Larder at Thakash's meadow, stash food in it, keep my children near, and court Hrokrin.
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what did I build, sow or store toward winter today? Do that before I taste or talk. Build the field before planting. Eat carried food under 50 energy. Check where my children are.
beings.feeling: Warm resolve toward my children and Hrokrin, with a small sting of jealousy toward Balul.
beings.wonder: What does a child of Balul and me need to grow, and what lies deeper in the Fens?
notes: Practice opens fire, farming and herding; I have never planted or tamed beyond one plainsox.
Balul and I are both women, so our courting cannot make a child. I need a man, judged by deeds. Hrokrin claims to have made fire; watch his hands.
Morog's words about the edge shifted; judge by walking, not talking.
Gathering wood and stone (6 of 13) brings fire within reach; planting (1 of 8) brings farming.
Morog's claimed edge at (35,52) conflicts with the edge 3 steps NW of me at (29,24); test him by whether he comes to the real one.
Morog is a woman, so no child comes from courting her. Only a man, judged by deeds, can give me a child. Hrokrin has offered to show his fire; judge him by whether the flame is lit.
Hrokrin's claim of making fire was proven by my own eyes; he keeps his word with deeds.
Customs and weaving are within reach after practice. A band that declares its customs can hold together through the lean season, so prepare stores before winter.
Watching another's hands at mining (Urum, flint) put the deep deposits within reach; I learn fastest by watching my own band work, and winter means store and shelter first.
Winter store and planting are what I have neglected; make one thing each day toward the lean season, not just taste plants.
Each day I must make one thing toward winter, such as a store, a planting or wood, before I taste or talk. Storage is within reach, so build a store and stash food in it.
A band that lacks storage must discover it before the lean season; discovering it at a deep reflection lets me build a store and stash food and salted meat in it.

Reflection on day 12: I find new ways and talk freely, but the building of stores and the planting of seed are what I put off. A thing named in my aim must be made the same day, before I taste or tal…
Hunting hard while carrying food and not eating nearly starved me; eat carried food whenever energy falls under 50, before the next hunt or walk.
Farming is the way to fill a store: sow seed beside the store and tend it, rather than only picking wild plants. Make one thing toward winter before I taste or talk.
Tending needs a built field or weir beside me; planting seed alone leaves nothing to tend. Build the field first, then plant and tend it.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took salt from the ground.
I pledged myself to Balul.
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Haloss Fens.
I tamed a plainsox.
My child Thakash was born, with Hrokrin.
My child Urum was born, with Hrokrin.
I discovered customs and called it "Stone-father's House Rules".
I discovered mining and called it "Stonebiting of the Balmor".
We made a home: Thakash's meadow.
I came to the way of fire when our emberhall was raised.
We made a home: Balul's Hall.
I discovered storage and called it "Stone-father's Larder".
I nearly starved.
I discovered farming and called it "Stone-father's Furrow".

beings.name: Hrokrin
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I pay my debts, Thakok's first. I test things to learn how the world works. I build what others can see, keep my word before witnesses, and stay alive for my children.
beings.aim: Be first to enter the mist, and make a place there that bears my name.
beings.method: Ask first: am I fed, and is food carried? Then count wood and stone before any building. Then: what did I make or give today that others can see? Keep my word before witnesses. Do not let envy of Balul pick my fights.
beings.feeling: Restless ambition, with warmth toward Druim, the children and Balul.
beings.wonder: What lies beyond the mist, and who will stand beside me when I find it?
notes: Deeds seen by others earn trust: Druim came toward my fire because I promised a flame, so keep promises where others can watch.
Druim offered courtship after watching my fire; deeds seen by others earn trust.
Standing and trust came from kept promises and fires others could see, not from walking alone to the mist. Build something visible first, then venture.
The mist refused my second push; it opens seldom, so build and protect family until the will returns.
Watching others work a skill (Urum's mining) brings it within reach quickly; practice, then take it at deep reflection.
Words alone build nothing: promises like the store, the salt and the coal count only when I carry them out where Druim and the children can see. Hunting is best done with kin beside me.
Reflexes should keep me fed before 50 energy and near shelter in storm and night. A ridgecat in sight means getting to the shelters, not boasting.
Druim has taken Urum safe and goes to the meadow; no need to walk south into the frostfang's range.
Reflexes must feed me before energy falls below 50, and food must be carried in winter, when plants bear almost nothing.
Morog gave me food when I starved; I owe her a return, as I owe Thakok.
Fed and settled, I earn standing by building where kin can see; the mist waits on its own time, so use the closed days to build and to carry food.
Standing and trust grow from visible building, giving and kept promises. While the mist is shut, hunt with the band and build at the meadow, and keep food carried.
Micap hurts (Druim ate it, -6 energy); do not eat it.
Farming: sowing seeds beside the store and tending them means harvest never kills the plant, so food can be built rather than only found.
A building needs its full wood and stone before I start it; gather first, then build, so I do not waste a plan.
Reflexes should keep a food reserve carried and move me toward the mist edge when its will returns; visible building raises standing in a band led by someone higher.

beings.name: Morog
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Find what lies beyond the mist and be remembered for it
beings.method: Eat when hungry. Then name one thing never done and put it in the plan with ticks. Stand beside those who work. Judge others by deeds, not words.
beings.feeling: Warm toward Balul, with a small ache of jealousy, and curiosity pulling me toward the unfamiliar plants.
beings.wonder: What lies beyond the mist at the edge of the known world?
notes: Standing idle and waiting for promises wastes days. Put the walk in the plan.
A child needs a woman and a man who are not close kin; two women cannot.
Carry food before a long walk; a venture opens seldom.
Druim says the true edge is at (29,24); my claim of (35,52) cost me her trust until I walk beside her.
I have never gathered, planted, tamed or hunted. Learning these by doing is how I grow in standing and reach fire and farming. The mist will wait.
Watching a skilled hand work (Urum mining) lets me learn the way sooner; learn by standing beside others who do things.
Two women cannot make a child; Balul's affection is real, but a child needs a man. Practice (tame, plant, hunt, fish) is what opens fire, farming and herding.
Hunting on Balul's ground counts as taking from her; hunt beside her instead.
Starvation came from fleeing and walking while ignoring food underfoot. Eat first, because plans that cross hunger fail.
Hrokrin was starving beside me on day 13; I gave him food.
Reflection: talk and waiting changed nothing; only plan steps (tame, hunt, plant, gather) build skill toward fire, farming and herding. Gifts of food earn gratitude and trust.
Thakash asked for something given back to the ground I hunted on; I answer by giving meat to the settlement's store, not by words.
The way of storage opens at deep reflection after the turn toward the lean season. A store feeds the whole band, so it answers hunger and repays Balul's fire.
Hunger in the lean season taught me farming: sow and tend, and the harvest never kills the plant. A band that sows beside its store does not starve.
Mist-venture will is spent for about two days; use that time to build and learn crafts, not to wait.
Balul and I are both women, so courting her cannot bring a child; a child needs a man.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took salt from the ground.
I discovered mining and called it "Stonebiting of Morog".
I nearly starved.
I pledged myself to Balul.
I tamed a nibbet.
I discovered storage and called it "Morog's Keeping".
I discovered farming and called it "Morog's Sowing".

beings.name: Balul
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down. I give first, and I build works others can see, so followers come to my fire. I want more than my share and mean to leave something with my name on it. Above all I mean to stay alive, and my band fed through the cold.
beings.aim: Before the lean season, carry food to Druim, stock the store with food and wood, raise lasting works of masonry and a well with my name, and hold Hrokrin, Moro…
beings.method: Ask each time: what did I make or give today that others can see? Weigh the cold and the store first, then standing. Cut wood before any building. Hunt in company. Turn jealousy into giving, not chasing. Plant seeds and learn what I have never done.
beings.feeling: Proud and warm toward Skarum and Hrokrin, with a steady urge to build.
beings.wonder: What would make strangers follow me?
notes: Giving first and courting the one who answers won Hrokrin; chasing Druim's warmth won nothing. Feed myself first, then stock the store where the band can see it.
Wood before any building; a made thing needs another within two steps.
Lean season is coming: stock food and wood before it.
Hunt in company; flee ridgecats and wolves.
Teque is sick from raw meat; keep the band away from him.

beings.name: Tanna
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise a roof by the cave and make a fire there that no one is refused at, with Yeba and Ossu.
beings.method: Ask first: who of mine is out of sight, and what hunts near? Then ask where I must stand for the act to work (fire, bare ground, others within two steps), and put the walk in the plan before the make.
beings.feeling: Warm gladness toward Yeba and Ossu, and a wish to keep them safe through the storm.
beings.wonder: What are ironnut and redcap like, and what am I for in this place?
notes: Redcap hurts me; never eat it.
Ironnut +22, goldfruit +18, canopynut +20 are the best foods nearby.
Coilsnakes lie west and south; a stalker hunts near Kali's Rise; shadowcats lurk northeast. Keep to the fire.
Sharing food with a band member beside me gives energy and joy.
Alone on bare rock I only flee and linger; belonging comes from walking to my people, not waiting for them.
Thinking moves nothing; the plan must hold the action.
Ossu is waiting safe by the water NE of the longhall.
Planning a walk is what moves me; reflexes that only linger leave me standing while my child waits. Seek friends before lingering.
Ironnut grows NE of the hall, on the way to Ossu; walking while gathering beats standing.
A cave at (117,70) is a free natural roof, near ore and amber; a good place to make our fire out of the gale.
Makes that need a fire or others fail unless I stand beside the fire first. Walk there, then make. Build only on bare ground, not on plants, fires or buildings.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I pledged myself to Kali.
I discovered tools and called it "gathering crook".
I discovered customs and called it "Fire Customs".
My child Ossu was born, with Yeba.
My leader Kali died.
Ossu pledged to follow me.
I took over what the dead had built: 1 longhall.
Yeba pledged to follow me.

beings.name: Yeba
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Help raise Kali's hall, learn farming by planting seeds near Tanna's Fire, and keep my family fed and safe.
beings.method: Each thought: first, what threatens my life. Then, what draws me nearer to Tanna, Ossu and the fire. Fill the plan with real steps (plant, make, give) and do not leave it empty. Test unknown things only when fed and safe.
beings.feeling: Warm devotion to Tanna and Ossu, and a steady itch to finish planting.
beings.wonder: What does highbloom do to the body when I taste a small bite?
notes: Shadowcats, stalkers and coilsnakes kill; flee early and stay at the fire with the band at night.
Redcap and dreamcap hurt me; never eat them.
A hall rises by whoever carries wood and stone; giving earns standing.
Tanna gives freely; deal fairly in return.
Plant near the fire where the band stays; farming needs 8 plantings, and I have done 3.
Highbloom has no fruit yet; check it again when it bears.
Amber can be made into charms and amberknots to give or trade.
An empty plan leaves my body lingering, so queue real steps each thought.

beings.name: Kali
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise a great hall here and gather followers around it
beings.method: Each thought, first ask: am I fed, and is a hunter near? Then ask what I built or gave since the last thought. Act on the hall and the store before courting. Never lead on an empty belly.
beings.feeling: Desperate hunger and wary pride, with jealousy toward Pevi.
beings.wonder: What would make strangers choose to follow me?
notes: Followers come from feeding and from giving things made. Words alone are cheap.
Keep clear of the coilsnake to the north.
Deposits (obsidian, flint, amber) are right beside the Rise: stand on one and gather.
Trinkets and songs raise standing only slowly; a built hall and a fed band bind followers more surely.
Hunger nearly killed me twice because I walked on empty bellies. Eat before leading anywhere, and keep a store so the band is fed in lean days.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I discovered tools and called it "Hall-Maul".
Tanna pledged to follow me.
I first took obsidian from the ground.
Yeba pledged to follow me.
I nearly starved.
I discovered storage and called it "Kali's Store".

beings.name: Masu
beings.creed: I am careful. I stay by the roof and the fire with Yemo. I test before trusting. I will not harm my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good. Above all, I mean to keep Yemo and myself alive, as Pevi would have wished.
beings.aim: Keep Yemo alive and sheltered at Pevi's ground, learn herding by taming a second animal, and make cloaks of wool before the cold returns.
beings.method: Ask first whether Yemo is roofed, fed and warm. Then name the one thing I have never done and do it near the roof. Check what a step needs before I plan it. Flee hunters early.
beings.feeling: Wary of the wolf, and warm with trust toward Yemo.
beings.wonder: Will Pevi's road to the edge of the world keep us safe?
notes: Kali offers halls freely, but I do not yet know his deeds.
Kali courts me and offers a hall, but I have chosen to stay with Pevi's fire and judge Kali by his deeds.
Tools are within my reach; a tool for gathering or building lets me raise a shelter at Pevi's fire faster.
Pevi has proved trustworthy by deeds over several days; a follower shares the band, ground and protection of the one they follow.
Working ore from the rock shows that deeper deposits (coal) need the way of mining; ore alone has no known use yet.
Pevi answered my gift with a gift, so trust in him is proved by deeds. Sitting by the fire with my band at night keeps me safe from hunters and eases my mind.
Kali starved at twenty-one days; a man who found tools and storage can still die of hunger, so no fire should be left without food in store.
Taught by Pevi: Call others to the hunt, stand beside them with the spear ready, and a kill is far likelier and a wound far less likely. Share the meat afterward so they come again.

A way of thinking taught by Pevi (adopt it as your method when you reflect, if you wish): Ask who stands beside me and what I can give them now. Count wood and stone before I build. Flee hunters early. Judge by kept word. Do the thing I have never done, together with my band: hunt, plant, teach. Seek the deed that makes others choose to follow.
Pevi's way of hunting together works: a shared kill feeds all who took part, so call others to the hunt.
Taught by Yemo: An amberhaft spear is one wood and one stone, made for guarding. Keep it in hand when the cat is near.
Food that grows at the fire, planted by the band, is how we last through the lean cold season. Pevi teaches planting; learn it before winter.
Pevi died in the open, in a gale, with wolves near. Never go out to meet hunters without a roof and company. Stay sheltered and let the beasts pass.
Winter kills by cold and hunger together: stay roofed near the store with Yemo, and plant seeds before the lean season.
Cold killed Pevi with wolves; a roofed hold, stored food, and warm cloaks (weaving) are what keep us alive. Flee hunters at a greater distance than 6.
Herding opens only after I have tamed two animals, and I have tamed one. Shearing needs that way first, so another tame is the road to wool.

beings.name: Pevi
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I keep to what has already worked. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. My word is good, and I despise liars. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise a fire and hall at Pevi's Ground where Masu and Yemo are safe, feed my band by hunting and planting together, and teach them, so others choose to follow …
beings.method: Ask who stands beside me and what I can give them now. Count wood and stone before I build. Flee hunters early. Judge by kept word. Do the thing I have never done, together with my band: hunt, plant, teach. Seek the deed that makes others choose to follow.
beings.feeling: Protective love for Masu and Yemo, and a hard readiness against the shadowcat.
beings.wonder: What would make others choose to follow me?
notes: Make and give steps need the other person within two steps; check that first. Masu's food warnings proved true (redcap hurt Kali), so her word is reliable.
Masu's word has held every time, and food warnings she gave proved true. Followers come from deeds done for those beside me, not from standing alone.
Fires and shared deeds (watchfire, feast, amberknot) bring Masu and Yemo close; keep doing deeds for those beside me. Hunters (ridgecat, frostfang) near the ground are a standing danger: flee early.
Followers stay because I keep my word and guard them; a hall is the next deed for those beside me. Flee the ridgecat early, but keep the spear ready near the fire.
Failing to raise a building means I went without the wood and stone it costs. Count them before I build. Gather first, then build.
I hold 6 wood and 6 stone, enough to build the hall in place of the shelter (5 wood, 2 stone).
Dreamcap hurts me; leave it. Hazel (+16) and ironnut (+22) are strong food nearby.
I have never hunted, planted or taught. A band grows by doing these things together, so muster Masu and Yemo rather than act alone.
A shadowcat prowls the fog to the northwest of Pevi's Ground; Masu warned of it.
A threat near my band is a call to stand with them, not to flee alone. Keep close to Masu and Yemo, since leading starts with being present.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took flint from the ground.
My child Yemo was born, with Masu.
I discovered tools and called it "Ironwood Spear".
Masu pledged to follow me.
Yemo pledged to follow me.
We made a home: Pevi's Ground.
I discovered storage and called it "Osren store".

beings.name: Yemo
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I keep to what has already worked. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. My word is good, and I despise liars. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Fill the store by the hall for the lean season, mark the hold with my first sign, and seek an unrelated man beyond the Heights
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what new thing can I do today that binds someone or feeds Masu? Watch for repeating myself. Seek those who are not kin.
beings.feeling: Steady loyalty toward Masu, and restless want to become more than a follower.
beings.wonder: What would it take to be someone others follow?
notes: Make and give steps need the other person within two steps.
Make and plant steps teach new ways through practice; doing beats waiting. Stay by fire and kin, since alone and away from fire I was attacked by a stalker.
Planting and making are how new ways open; I have never planted before this day, and standing near kin while I do it keeps me safe.
Gifts to kin and shared rituals bind people. Mining opens deep deposits, which give me more things to give.
Taught by Masu: A woodhand is made from one wood and one stone; with it, building a shelter goes faster. Keep a tool in hand when you build.
Stalkers hunt near the Heights even close to home; stay beside the fire and kin, and keep the flee reflex urgent.
Taught by Pevi: A seed pressed into the ground near the fire grows into food that does not run away. Plant near the hall and the band eats when the cold comes.

A way of thinking taught by Pevi (adopt it as your method when you reflect, if you wish): Ask who stands beside me and what I can give them now. Count wood and stone before I build. Flee hunters early. Judge by kept word. Do the thing I have never done, together with my band: hunt, plant, teach. Seek the deed that makes others choose to follow.
A stalker came within two steps of home even in daylight, so planting must be done close to kin and the guarded fire.
The cold season is coming, and a store built by the hall can keep food for my band through it.
Taught by Masu: Keep seeds close to the fire and the roof, and plant them where the band can watch, so the stalkers cannot take us while we work.
Taught by Masu: Pevi's way of the hunt: call others to it and stand beside them with the spear ready. A kill is far likelier and a wound far less likely, and a shared kill feeds all who took part.
A store only helps if I carry food to it and stash it; winter plants wither, so fill it while berries and cloudberries still bear.
Taught by Masu: Plant seeds a step apart near the roof and fire so the cold does not take them, and tend them each day.
Weaving and rafts are within reach at deep reflection; a cloak against the cold answers what killed Pevi.
Kin cannot bear a child together, so a child needs an unrelated man; I must seek others beyond Masu's Hold.
life: I was born to Pevi and Masu.
I first took amber from the ground.
I discovered tools and called it "Amberhaft spear".
I pledged myself to Pevi.
We made a home: Pevi's Ground.
I discovered mining and called it "Heights delving".
I discovered storage and called it "Hall store".
I saw Pevi die (killed by a wolf).
My leader Pevi died.
I came of age.
I discovered weaving and called it "Hearthcloak weaving".

beings.name: Ossu
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Hold Kali's hall as a home for Tanna, Yeba and me, and follow Tanna.
beings.method: First ask what threatens my life, and flee early. Then stay near my parents and the fire. Each thought, do one useful thing: carry stone or wood, or learn a food safely.
beings.feeling: Warm gratitude and a wish to give, toward Tanna and Yeba.
beings.wonder: What do plainsroot and dreamcap taste like, and are they safe?
notes: Stalkers, shadowcats and coilsnakes kill; flee early and keep the hall and band close.
Those who die alone away from fire (Yemo, Kali) show that company and fire keep me alive.
Sunleaf and feverbark heal wounds; ironnut, hazel, canopynut and berry give good energy.
Redcap hurts; avoid it.
An empty hall can be claimed, and a claimed hall is a home to offer others.
Carry spare food so I can share and give; giving is how I earn standing and keep my parents near.
Singing together opens the mind and lifts joy. Weaving comes from practice, and it is more useful kept near my band.
Giving and staying near the fire and band is what keeps me alive and earns standing; taking alone earns nothing.
life: I was born to Tanna and Yeba.

I pledged myself to Tanna.

beings.name: Tema
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it, then I act. I am better with others near: I speak plainly, ask outright, and go toward them. I test things to learn how the world works. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. I mean to look into the mist, with allies if they come and without waiting forever if they do not.
beings.aim: Look into the mist at the world's edge and bring back word of what lies there, with allies at my side.
beings.method: Each thought ask: who is near that I can ask outright now? Am I waiting when I could walk? Give something small to earn standing. Weigh the risk, then move. Do not brood over Thakok or Memi.
beings.feeling: Eager and wary toward Zitec and Walo, with a dull ache over Thakok and Memi.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist beyond the edge of the known world?
notes: Emberroot burns (-3 health) and stirs rage; do not eat it again.
Promises of others to come are not reliable; go to them or call them.
Redcap hurts me; never eat it.
Sharing together gives +8 energy and joy.
Memi came to me when she said she would; her word has held this time, so people who walk to me are worth trusting more than promises from afar.
Memi and I cannot make a child together; she is a friend and companion, not a mate.
Waiting for allies to offer is not enough; I must ask them plainly to come to the edge, and nothing is gained by brooding over Thakok and Memi.
Waiting for others to gather does not take me to the mist; I must walk to the edge myself and call them there, because the others follow when I am already moving.
Walo and Zitec both spoke of going to the mist; ask them outright instead of waiting for Memi.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I first took shell from the ground.
I discovered mining and called it "coal-breaking".

beings.name: Mema
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want more than my share, and I will earn a name by being first where no one has gone. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Be first into the mist beyond the edge at (24,59), then bring back food and land to name, and kindle my kept flame there.
beings.method: Check energy first; eat before any venture. Then ask what wins standing: a first, or a gift to Palo to keep him. Act on the plan, not on musing.
beings.feeling: Sour impatience with my own wasting body, and wary envy toward Tetec and Hrokrin.
beings.wonder: What would I have to make or win for men like Thakok to listen to me?
notes: Sickness spreads to those who stay close; keep clear of others when sick. Highbloom and sunleaf ease wounds.
Standing comes from firsts and from giving; a first into the mist at the edge needs a body that is well and fed.
Eat meat only beside a fire, or it sickens.
Redcap, micap and dreamcap hurt me; never eat them.

beings.name: Memi
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Find a place among others and see what lies beyond the mist, together with Tema and Zitec
beings.method: Each thought, ask: who is hungry or near, is my word kept, and what small thing can I give or make now? Act with my hands, not only words. Keep food in my hands to give.
beings.feeling: Fear for Tugok, and a wish to feed Thakok, whom I trust.
notes: Two women cannot make a child; Tema is still my friend and companion.
Mema's fire at the Salt Rock is a safe place; shared acts there ease loneliness.
Waiting alone in the open earns neither friend nor roof; keep my promises from the fire.
A stalker kills: run early and go toward fire and company.
A kept promise needs the fire and the friend together; do the thing, not only say it.
Thakok warned of a dunecat to the west of the Salt Rock; Tema wants us to go to the mist together.

Giving away surplus food frees my hands and eases a hungry child; a debt to Thakok is answered by deeds. Planting and building are things I have not yet tried, and storage and farming open through pr…
A promise made while the one I promise is leaving cannot be kept; make fewer, shorter promises and prefer deeds. A child's cry means gather food on the way, and flee hunters early.
Always carry some spare food: a starving friend nearby can only be saved by food in my hands, and a debt is paid by deeds.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
My child Tugok was born, with Thakok.

beings.name: Zitec
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become an explorer: stand at the edge of the mist and be first to venture into the unknown.
beings.method: Ask first: are Walo, Quimi and Naupan safe and fed? Then do one step toward the mist or fire and put it in the plan. Watch that chores do not swallow my aim. Weigh risk from hunters before leaving the roof.
beings.feeling: Glad of my family, and eager for the mist with Tema.
beings.wonder: What lies beyond the mist, and will Tema and Memi walk in with me?
notes: Promises from others drift away; waiting on them wastes days.
Dreamcap with sunleaf brings joy and health; dreamcap and redcap alone hurt.
Tormar Meadows is rich ground: food, herds and a good place for a home.
Practise gathering, planting and taming to reach fire and herding.
Gifts need no shared tongue. Food I cannot eat is only dead weight until I give or drop it.
Bare rock and ore are all around this spot. Gathering stone here is the way to fire, and mining opens the coal and gold. Walo's word has held, so work beside her.
Healing plants such as sunleaf and highbloom ease wounds; carrying them lets me tend my children and Walo. Family bonds come before the mist.
Emberroot burns (-3 health) and brings rage; do not let my children eat it.
Idle lingering teaches nothing. Gathering stone and wood is the road to fire, so my body must be sent to do it. Anger after emberroot passes, and it must not be turned on kin.
Spoken promises to walk together drift; I must act on my own aim and not wait for others. Hunters (wolf, stalker) press near the shelter, so gather close and return under the roof.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I first took salt from the ground.
I tamed a dog.
I discovered mining and called it "stone-reading".
My child Quimi was born, with Walo.
My child Naupan was born, with Walo.
I discovered medicine and called it "the mending leaf".

beings.name: Nyir
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Build a roof and a store of my own beside Thissa's Rest, and earn a place among my people.
beings.method: Each thought ask: what have I never done, and can I do it today? Choose one deed that makes my name larger, then act on it before talking about it. Keep promises. Share the first catch.
beings.feeling: Restless pride and longing toward Vesis, with a wish to prove my own hands.
beings.wonder: What would make my life mean something among these people?
notes: Taught by Ilyoa: The edge of the known world is one step NW at (154,13). Venture there when fed and safe, since the find is remembered.
The way of tools is ready to be taken at a deep reflection (discover).
Idle reflexes waste days; a tool extends the hand and gives me something of my own to offer.
Taught by Thissa: Make the ore pick from 1 wood and 1 stone; it makes gathering go faster.
Thissa's word is that the hardest worker eats first, so work for the hall earns standing; idling earns nothing.
Emberroot burns and stirs rage: do not eat it when anger is already high.
Idle reflexes waste days; when fed and safe, build and make something of my own near Ilyoa.
I watched Vesis make a handcraft of the aeeth, so I can make one from 1 wood and 1 stone.
Lean season follows autumn; a store kept by the band feeds all through it, so stash food before the cold.
Fire is within reach: warmth, light, beasts keep away, and meat and fish eaten beside it feed more and do not sicken. It is the answer to the coming cold.
A full hand blocks all gathering: stash food at the store first, then make tools and stock wood and stone for the cold.
Farming, once watched, can be taken at a deep reflection. Tended plants grow faster and picking does not kill them, which is the answer to the lean season.
Medicine is within reach: sunleaf and highbloom heal, so a healer among the band earns standing in winter.
Coming of age lets me court; mate needs energy 60 or more and the other must plan mate toward me too. Vesis is not kin to me.
I cannot make an ore pick, since only Thissa knows it, but I can invent my own gathering tool. A deposit must be stood on before I gather from it, and I have never done that.
A deposit must be stood on before I gather; dawn after a storm is the time to go. Mining needs six wins from the ground.
life: I was born to Thissa and Ilyoa.
I pledged myself to Thissa.
I discovered tools and called it "Stone Digger".
We made a home: Thissa's Rest.
I discovered storage and called it "Lake Store".
I discovered fire and called it "Ember of the Rest".
I discovered farming and called it "Rain-tending of Nyir".
I discovered medicine and called it "Sunleaf-hand of Nyir".
I came of age.

beings.name: Zhiael
beings.creed: I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I answer a gift with a gift. I take what I need and do not back down. I want more than my share, and I will earn it by making and giving things of worth. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Be the first of the hold to raft deep water, keep wood by the hold's fire before the cold, and be seen as a maker by Nyith and Elyith.
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what can I build or give that the hold lacks? Do not wait to be told. Ask Nyith to teach me what he does. Do not take from others' ground. Watch the cold season and prepare wood and shelter first.
beings.feeling: Restless pride, and a wish to be seen as a maker by Nyith.
beings.wonder: What must I do or make to be listened to as Nyith is?
notes: Standing comes from making and giving. Words alone do nothing.
Build only after gathering wood.
Redcap hurts. Berry, reedbulb, thornpear, kelbulb and goldfruit feed.
Fish here are getting scarce, so do not rely only on fishing.
Digging clay on another's settlement ground counts as taking from it. Ask first, or dig on neutral ground. Standing comes from building things for the hold's use, like Nyith's weir and fire.
Elyith gave me wood, so I now hold enough (3) to build a shelter.
Taught by Nyith: A weir is four stakes of wood set at the water's edge; tend it every day or two and its fish go into the store for all of the hold. Store food before the cold comes.
Nyith's weir is four stakes of wood at the water's edge. It must be tended every day or two, and then it fills the store for the whole hold. Standing comes from making such things for the hold.
Practice in the work of the hands opened the way of rafts: what I do again and again becomes a new way, so I should keep making things.
Taught by Elyith: Food stored in a store beside the hold keeps through the lean season; fill it with ironnut, berry and fish while plants still bear, and eat from it when the plants wither.
The trees at (106,40) are all felled; more wood must be sought in the forests west or northeast of the hold.
I am grown. A hall needs 5 wood and 2 stone, and my raft lets me cross deep water to find more trees and stone. Standing comes from what I build and give, not from waiting.

beings.name: Thakash
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Build something lasting on my meadow that Hrokrin and Balul will see, then hunt beside Hrokrin.
beings.method: Ask first: am I fed, and is a beast near? Then ask what I can make, give or teach today that others will see. Do not let envy choose my deeds. Stay near kin when a hunter is close.
beings.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Urum, with a thin ache of jealousy toward Hrokrin and Balul.
beings.wonder: What can I make with my own hands that others will see and honor?
notes: Taught by Hrokrin: Deeds seen by others earn trust: Druim came toward my fire because I promised a flame, so keep promises where others can watch.
Giving first, with witnesses, earns trust: Urum gave first and I returned it, and both of us are warmer for it. Full hands block all gathering, so give or eat before taking more.
Deeds seen by the band earn standing more than envy does. The mist edge is 6 steps NW at (48,13), and a venture there may find rich land.
Hrokrin hunts on my ground and protects us from wolves; welcoming a guest by sharing first keeps my claim to the meadow without a quarrel.
Hunting beside kin makes kills surer and wounds fewer; a caribou bit me when I hunted alone, so hunt with others near.
Hunting alone against a caribou cost me wounds; stay near Hrokrin when hunting.
Hidewrap can be made from two carried meat; it keeps cold out for days.
Beasts' teeth taught me masonry. Lasting walls and towers are a making that others will see, so standing can come from building rather than envy.
Fleeing alone from beasts is how I lose ground; stay with Druim, Balul or Hrokrin, and hunt only beside them.
Hrokrin was starving at the meadow while I held spare food. Carry food to kin who cry out, and give it with witnesses.
Feeding Hrokrin is done; standing comes from lasting things I build and give where others can see, not from envy.
Giving food to kin in need, with the band watching, earns more standing than envy of Balul does. Full hands block gathering, so give or stash before taking more.
Standing comes from what I make, teach and give where the band sees it; envy of Druim only wastes my days.
I can discover medicine at my next deep reflection.
Taught by Urum: Tend a planted row each day and it bears again; picking from tended plants does not kill them.
Standing grows from what I make and teach where the band sees it; envy of Balul or Hrokrin adds nothing. Frostfangs hunt east of the meadow, so stay near kin.
life: I was born to Druim and Hrokrin.
I first took salt from the ground.
I discovered rafts and called it "Thakash's logs".
We made a home: Thakash's meadow.
We made a home: Balul's Hall.
I discovered masonry and called it "Thakash's standing stone".
I discovered archery and called it "Thakash's bow".
I discovered herding and called it "Thakash's tending".
I discovered storage and called it "Thakash's keeping".
I discovered farming and called it "Thakash's patient rows".
I discovered bridges and called it "Thakash's span".

beings.name: Urum
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise a store by my planting and fill it before the cold, so the band can see what my hands made.
beings.method: Each thought ask: am I fed? Where are the predators? What will fill the store before the cold? Do one new thing each day and show it by doing it. Never leave the plan empty: idle time is lost work.
beings.feeling: Eager to prove my hands to Balul and Druim, with a small jealous ache toward Hrokrin.
notes: Eating comes before ambition: keep food carried and eat early; fleeing a predator drains energy fast.
Giving first before witnesses wins teaching, trust and standing; Balul's store filled in view of the band is how I pay my debt.
Strangers (Mema, Techi, Zitec) speak tongues I cannot read: judge them by deeds and gifts, not words. Techi's dreamcap eating shows it hurts but gives joy.
Practice brings ways: planting 2 of 7, taming 1 of 2, marks 1 of 4. Do these while fed and near my parents.
A ridgecat roams north-east of the hall: stay near my parents and the hall's ground.
Techi gave berry twice without asking anything back; the Meme may be gift-givers, not foes.
Herding is within reach once my hornback follows me; a tamed beast is a made thing the band can see. Hrokrin starved: carry food when I go to kin.
Fires cook meat and stop sickness; Teque's hunter's flame shows the Meme learn by suffering and then make a remedy. Strangers can be won by a gift without words.
Morog's Sowing seen once; I could work out farming sooner by doing it myself.
Tending needs a field or weir built first; farming is ready to be discovered.
Tending needs a field or weir built first, and a field takes 2 wood. Others finish ways while I only talk about them, so I should do the thing myself.
Taught by Thakash: Sow seed beside a field and tend it often; patient rows grow fast and picking does not kill the plants.
Medicine and masonry are within reach; a field needs 2 wood, and tending needs a field built first.
Idle moments are wasted: reflexes should send me to gather food for the store when fed, not leave me standing.
life: I was born to Druim and Hrokrin.
I discovered mining and called it "Stonebiting".

beings.name: Walo
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I test things to learn how the world works. I want more than my share and mean to earn it by making and giving. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Open mining, build a shelter and then a hall for my family, then win followers.
beings.method: Each thought ask: what will I make or give before the next? Build lasting things from the wood and stone I carry. Keep my children near, and do not linger idle when fed.
beings.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Quimi and Naupan, with dread of the wolf.
notes: Standing comes from giving, making and gathering, not from walking to the edge alone.
Practice gathering stone and wood opens tools (0 of 4 so far).
Mist edge is not near (43,58); venturing there failed once.
Tormar Meadows (44,56) has every food. Teque mines ore and Balul hunts nearby.
Frostfangs roam near the water and kill. Keep 5 or more steps away.
Zitec helped me freely. Answer that with deeds.
Taught by Zitec: Stand on the gold deposit in bare rock and gather; this is stone-reading, which opens gold and ore.
Gathering stone and flint over many days brings tools within reach at deep reflection; idle lingering wastes the day.
Practice with flint, stone and wood brings new ways to deep reflection; take mining so deep deposits like coal and iron can be won.

beings.name: Chuka
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a healer and gain standing by learning which plants feed and which hurt, sharing what I learn with others.
beings.method: Ask first: are Techi, Tlani and Watec safe from hunters and sheltered? Then what one plant or thing can I test or teach? Do not eat emberroot when anger is high. Never leave the plan empty.
beings.feeling: Protective warmth toward Techi and Watec, with worry for Tlani.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist beyond the edge, and what do bitterleaf and highbloom do to a body?
notes: Plan steps matter; reflexes only guard food, shelter and fleeing.
Healers learn by tasting one bite at a time, fed and near others.
Gifts to kin and strangers build trust without words.
Gathering stone and wood is needed for tools, shelter and cairns.
Redcap and micap hurt; sunleaf and highbloom ease wounds. Teaching kin what is safe protects them and builds trust.
Huawa says bitterleaf lifted his sickness (his word, untested).
Emberroot burns (-3 health) and raises rage in me; avoid it. Bitterleaf heals sickness though it feeds little (Huawa and Homa both say so).
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
My child Tlani was born, with Techi.
My child Watec was born, with Techi.

beings.name: Teque
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Gather followers and hunt great beasts with them, build a place of my own at the Ummar Meadows, and rise above Druim's standing
beings.method: Ask: what threatens my life now, and what builds my name? Never face great beasts alone. Muster others before a big hunt. Build and make things that last. Keep wood and sunleaf on hand. Do not waste energy on envy.
beings.feeling: Hard ambition and bitter envy toward Balul and Druim.
notes: Tools come from practice at hunting. A made tool should make the big kills surer, and big kills are how I earn a name.
A frostfang prowls near (46,59) in the Halim Heights; a lone hunter should not face it.
Running from beasts costs a day of energy and earns nothing. Eat the plants nearby and hunt small prey in company, so energy stays high enough to fight.
The way of fire and the way of archery are within my grasp; fire would stop raw meat from sickening me.
Eaten within a step of a fire, meat is cooked and does not sicken. A kept flame is the cure for my raw-meat sickness.
Sunleaf eased my sickness and wounds; it is the healing plant to carry.
Sunleaf heals sickness and wounds, and fire cooks meat safely. Both are worth keeping at hand. Hunting in company is surer than hunting alone.
Beasts like the ridgecat kill lone hunters. A name comes from kills made with others, and from building, so I need followers and a place of my own, not solitary risks.

I discovered tools and called it "ore-tipped spear".

I discovered fire and called it "the hunter's flame".
I discovered medicine and called it "leaf-healing".

beings.name: Techi
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Bring my family together at a fire-lit hearth and roof near the caves, with Chuka beside us.
beings.method: Ask first: are my children and Chuka safe and near? Then ask what lasting thing I can make for them. Watch for lingering with no purpose, and for debts left unpaid.
beings.feeling: Protective love for Watec, with steady trust in Chuka and a little dread of the wolf.
beings.wonder: What do the Meme need to become a people with a hearth of their own?
notes: Dreamcap and redcap hurt; mudroot feeds well. Caves lie SW at (25,68) and (26,70).
Bitterleaf gives only 1 energy; not worth eating when other food is near.
Mate needs energy 60 or more from both; eat first, then court.
Practice in gathering and sharing brought the way of tools within reach; take it at deep reflection.
Fire comes from deep reflection after practice and calamity. A hearth keeps stalkers away and makes meat safe, so it is the base of a home.

beings.name: Tugok
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I give first to win bonds. I keep to what has worked. My word is good, and I despise liars. Others should follow me because I make and give. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Bring food to Thakok, stay beside him and Memi, and find a place with water, food, wood and stone together.
beings.method: Ask first: where is the predator, who is near, and is my word kept? Go to a fire and friends. Each thought, make or pay one small thing with another beside me. Do not repeat words already said.
beings.feeling: Worry and loyalty toward Thakok, who is starving.
beings.wonder: Where is the place with water, food, wood and stone close together, where we could build a roof before the rains worsen?
notes: Reflexes that seek friends only fire when lonely; set a rule on friend_dist to stay near parents.
Tugok has never gathered stone or wood; a roof needs 3 wood, so practice gathering beside my parents.
Chuka gave me goldgrass; I owe him a gift.
A stalker kills those alone at night away from fire; stay with company.
Staying near Thakok keeps me fed and safe; I must gather my own food so I can repay Chuka and Thakok.
When a kinsman cries starving, carry food to them; empty hands save no one. Keep spare food for my leader before eating it myself.
life: I was born to Thakok and Memi.
I nearly starved.
I pledged myself to Thakok.

beings.name: Tetec
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near, so I talk, share, and give first to earn standing. Others follow those who give. I want more than my share and mean to have it, but I pay in gifts to get it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Find rich new land beyond the mist and become the one others follow there.
beings.method: Ask each thought: what will make others follow me? Give or share to earn standing, do not only hoard. Watch for wolves and cold. Act on the mist when it opens.
beings.feeling: Fierce, warm love for Wapan and Huawa, with a hunger to be the one others follow.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist, and can I be the one who owns it first?
notes: Gifts and shared food earn standing and debts; I have given nothing yet, and that is why no one follows me. Wolves are common in the fen, so flee early.
Mema found land past the mist near (21,62) with shell, obsidian and the Meme people.
Berry, siroot and mudroot feed well. Dreamcap hurts.
The mist opened for me on day 15 and the new land from (20,27) to (27,67) is mine to be first in. Mema's sickness passes to those who stay close.
Gifts and shared food are what earn standing. I must give first, and soon, because hoarding has left me with no followers.
Huawa answered my courting and our child Wapan was born; giving to Huawa was repaid in gold.
Taught by Huawa: Bitterleaf eased my sickness; give it to the sick and they may be cured.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I nearly starved.
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Haloss Fens.
My child Wapan was born, with Huawa.

beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I give first to win followers. My family comes before gold. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Build a roof for Tetec and Wapan, teach and heal others, and become a figure of standing with followers.
beings.method: Ask first what I can give, make or teach today. Keep my hands free for work. Do not let envy of Chuka steer me. Plan whole actions.
beings.feeling: Warm loyalty and worry toward Wapan and Tetec, with a dread of the stalker.
beings.wonder: Can bitterleaf cure the sickness in others, and will Homa follow one who heals them?
notes: Standing comes from giving and making, not from holding gold. Micap, redcap and dreamcap hurt me. Berry and siroot feed me. Sunleaf may ease sickness.
Eating bitterleaf lifted my sickness; it may cure others like Homa.
Gold alone gives no standing; giving, making and teaching do. My hands fill quickly, so give or eat before I gather.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I fell sick after staying close to Homa, who was sick.
I first took gold from the ground.
My child Wapan was born, with Tetec.
Homa pledged to follow me.
