records.thought: Balul is a woman and so am I, so my courting led nowhere. The longing for a child will have to wait for a man, and it need not sour what Balul and I are to each other. Hrokrin is near and close to her, and the jealousy burns, but he fed me kindness on day 13 and I judge by deeds. I have never tasted gorsemint or brugoldgrass, and both grow 11 steps SW. Going there is something new I can do while the mist-will rests, and I can eat there rather than carry food.
records.feeling: Warm toward Balul, with a small ache of jealousy, and curiosity pulling me toward the unfamiliar plants.

records.text: Tanna led "sharing" with Yeba.

records.name: Walo
records.text: Quimi, stay beside me. I am going to build a roof for us all, and then you can show me what you make with your ore.
Walo rewrote its own way of thinking.
Walo discovered mining: "deep-delving" — Strike the rock with a flint-edge pick to break deep seams of coal, iron and ore, and to win shallow deposits faster..

records.name: Walo
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering and wandering near the children, and I am fed and glad, but nothing I have made will outlast me and no one follows me. Zitec is my trust, and his rage passes. Thakok still gnaws at me, but my children and Zitec come first. Mining is within my reach, and coal and iron lie deep, so I take it. Then I will build a shelter and hall with the wood and stone I carry, so that I make something lasting.
records.feeling: Fierce resolve and warm pride toward Zitec and my children.

say.text: Quimi, stay beside me. I am going to build a roof for us all, and then you can show me what you make with your ore.

changes: set its aim: "Open mining, build a shelter and then a hall for my family, then win followers."

records.text: Walo built a shelter.

records.name: Tetec
records.text: Huawa, you gave me gold when you were sick, and I remember it. Come to me. I will bring food, and we will make something that outlasts us both.
Tetec rewrote its own reflexes.
Tetec rewrote its creed.

records.name: Tetec
records.thought: I have spent my days eating and drifting, and I have given nothing to anyone. That is why no one follows me. Huawa gave me gold when he was sick, and I owe him. He is the one I want a child with, and he holds 5 food while I hold none. Chuka's standing is 3.5 against my 0.9, so I must earn standing by giving and by being first in the mist, not by waiting. I am fed now, so I will gather food to carry and then give some to Huawa and court him.
records.feeling: Wanting Huawa near, and hungry for standing over Chuka.

say.text: Huawa, you gave me gold when you were sick, and I remember it. Come to me. I will bring food, and we will make something that outlasts us both.

records.name: Druim
records.thought: My hands are full of plainsroot while my seeds sit unsown, and this ground is already taken by Urum's field, so I must stop circling. I will put the roots into the Larder one step away, which empties my hands and feeds my children's winter. Then I will find bare ground, west where there is rock and clay, and raise my own field so my seeds go in the earth. Hrokrin is near and glad, and the jealousy over Balul can wait while I make something toward winter.
records.feeling: Warm resolve toward my children and Hrokrin, with a sting of jealousy toward Balul.

records.text: Naupan led "sharing" with Zitec.

records.name: Skarum
records.thought: Balul stands high and Druim sits close to her while I am small and carry nothing, and it burns, but a child who picks a fight loses it. Druim's store holds 20 food and I have given nothing yet in my whole life; a gift others can see is what lifts standing. I will gather food from the frostmoss and rimewort to the south and bring it back to give to Balul before witnesses.
records.feeling: Envious and hungry to be noticed, mostly toward Balul and Druim.

records.name: Teque
records.thought: Balul's people have a hall, a field and a store with twenty food, and I have a shelter I did not build and a spear I cannot even remake without wood. Envy of Druim eats at me, but my own rule says to build and make things that last, so I will stop gnawing and start. The ridgecat to the SW kills lone hunters, so I will not go near it. I will take wood and stone from the forest, then raise a shelter and a mark of my own at the Ummar Meadows, where the herds will gather.
records.feeling: Hard ambition and bitter envy toward Balul and Druim.

came.why: What you have practised has come together. The way of weaving is with…

records.name: Huawa
records.text: Tetec, I am Huawa and I keep my word. I am coming to you with gold and bitterleaf. Let us build a roof against this storm and make something that lasts.

records.name: Huawa
records.thought: Storm and cold gnaw at me, and Tetec has called me to make something that outlasts us both. That is the first real offer of a follower or partner, and I gave gold first, as my creed says. Techi still stings, but Tetec is strong, has standing 0.9, and remembers my gift, so I go to Tetec and mark my word by gathering the gold near me to give and make. Homa is owed, but Homa already has the bitterleaf I promised, so I will repay with deeds later.
records.feeling: Steady hope toward Tetec, and a dull envy of Chuka over Techi.

say.text: Tetec, I am Huawa and I keep my word. I am coming to you with gold and bitterleaf. Let us build a roof against this storm and make something that lasts.

records.name: Zitec
records.text: Naupan, your gold is fairly dug and I will trade you a stone for it. Then go to the shelter with Walo and Quimi, out of the storm.

records.name: Zitec
records.thought: My children are near and fed, Walo has raised a roof, and the storm is cold on my back. The old anger is thin now, and the gnawing over Druim I will not feed. Naupan offers gold for stone, and a fair trade honors what my child dug with their own hands, so I will accept it. Then I will taste the brugoldgrass to the southwest, since I have never known it, and bring Quimi's cairn-warmth with me to the shelter, for the mist can wait until my family is dry and rested.
records.feeling: Steady gladness toward my children and Walo, with a curious itch toward the unknown brugoldgrass.

say.text: Naupan, your gold is fairly dug and I will trade you a stone for it. Then go to the shelter with Walo and Quimi, out of the storm.

plan: trade [name Naupan, what stone, want gold] (10 moments)

records.text: Zitec and Naupan traded stone for gold.

records.name: Naupan
records.text: Walo, Quimi, stand close by me. I have stone, and I will raise a cairn for us all. Then I will give each of you some of my gold.

records.name: Naupan
records.thought: Zitec's weight still burns in me, yet he walked through the storm for me, and Walo built this roof. Gold has bought me nothing so far, but I can make something with my hands: Walo and Quimi are beside me and I hold stone, so I will lead a cairn and give them something that binds us. That is honest standing, earned by giving. Then I will shelter from the cold and gather flint, so I can make a pick and keep making.
records.feeling: Warm toward Zitec and Walo, still stung by jealousy, eager to give something of my own.

say.text: Walo, Quimi, stand close by me. I have stone, and I will raise a cairn for us all. Then I will give each of you some of my gold.

records.text: Naupan led "cairn" with Tema, Walo, Quimi.
Quimi discovered fire: "Fenhearth" — A kept flame fed with wood and struck from flint and stone, giving warmth and light and keeping beasts at a distance, and cooking meat so it feeds more and neve.

records.name: Quimi
records.thought: I have spent my days near Walo and Zitec, giving gold and ore and wanting to be weighed as they are weighed. The jealousy is real, but standing comes from making and giving, not from sulking. I hold stone and ore, and the way of fire is within my reach, so I take it now. Then I will make something to give Walo and Zitec.
records.feeling: Restless pride and warmth toward Walo, with a sting of jealousy toward Zitec.
changes: restated something it already knew (not written down again)
set its aim: "Learn fire, then make flint talismans and give one to Walo and one to Zitec."

records.text: Naupan gave a gold to Walo.

records.name: Tema
records.text: Walo, Zitec, I am Tema. You both said you go to the mist's edge. The edge is a few steps NW of me. Come with me now and we go in together, sharing food as we go.
Tema rewrote its own way of thinking.
Tema discovered mining: "coal-breaking" — Break deep stone with flint-edged hands to win coal and ore..

records.name: Tema
records.thought: I have said I would go to the mist, and I have wandered, dropped food and stood idle while Memi and Thakok gnaw at me. Memi has my trust and Thakok my ache, but neither is here, and I have never made, given or hunted anything, so my standing stays small. Walo, Zitec and the children stand together nine steps east, and both Walo and Zitec have said they want the mist too. I should go to them and ask outright, then give them something to start earning trust. Coal and flint lie close, and mining is within my reach, so I will take it up.
records.feeling: Eager and a little restless, toward Walo and Zitec as possible allies.

say.text: Walo, Zitec, I am Tema. You both said you go to the mist's edge. The edge is a few steps NW of me. Come with me now and we go in together, sharing food as we go.

records.name: Vesis
records.text: Ilyoa, I will sow here beside you now. Let us court as well, if your heart is free.
Vesis rewrote its own way of thinking.
Vesis discovered medicine: "Lake-balm" — Carry sunleaf and highbloom and press them to wounds to ease them, for myself and for others..

records.name: Vesis
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, sitting in halls and aching over Thissa while following Ilyoa about. None of it has made a field or a child. I have learned fire and weaving, yet I have nothing of my own standing in the ground. Thissa has a child with Ilyoa, and I will not let jealousy steer me. Ilyoa is near and says she keeps her word, so I will work beside her and court her openly. The cold season is coming, so healing plants matter, and I know sunleaf and highbloom mend wounds. I will name that knowledge as medicine, then drop my hands' load into the store and build the field.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Ilyoa, with a quiet ache over Thissa.

say.text: Ilyoa, I will sow here beside you now. Let us court as well, if your heart is free.

records.text: Vesis is courting Ilyoa.

records.name: Homa
records.thought: I am fed, and the storm and the night are cold, but I am alone out here on bare rock when Huawa said he was bringing me bitterleaf and I trust him most of anyone. Sapcane is three steps northwest and I have never tasted it. That would answer my curiosity cheaply, and then I can carry some to share, since a band is built from food given and kept promises. Then I will go toward Huawa and Chuka, where the others are, rather than sit alone in the storm.
records.feeling: Warm hope toward Huawa, and a restless wish to taste the sapcane.

records.text: Tetec gave kelbulb to Huawa.
Huawa gave a gold to Tetec.

records.name: Walo
records.text: Quimi, Naupan, Zitec, stay near. I am raising a hall over this shelter, so that our family has a great roof and the Mother's hearth has a home.
Walo named a place "Walo's Hearth".

records.name: Walo
records.thought: I stand in my own shelter with my children and Zitec near, and the storm cannot touch us. I have wood 3 and stone 6, and a hall costs little since the shelter is used again, so I will raise it now and give my family a great roof that bears my name. Then I can go on to coal and win followers, because nothing I have made yet will outlast me.
records.feeling: Fierce resolve and warm pride toward my children and Zitec.

say.text: Quimi, Naupan, Zitec, stay near. I am raising a hall over this shelter, so that our family has a great roof and the Mother's hearth has a home.

records.text: Tetec is courting Huawa.
Huawa answered Tetec's courting.
Wapan was born to Tetec and Huawa.

records.name: Zitec
records.thought: The plan I have is good: finish the berries, walk south to the brugoldgrass and taste it, and so answer the itch that has gnawed at me. My children are fed and near the shelter with Walo, and Tema calls us to the mist's edge, which is my own aim, so I will not let it slip behind gathering again. I will taste first, then go find Tema and ask how far the edge lies, and bring the children no nearer to danger than the shelter.
records.feeling: Curious gladness toward the unknown grass, and warmth toward my children and Walo.

came.why: Tema said to everyone nearby: "Walo, Zitec, I am Tema. You both said …

records.name: Ilyoa
records.text: Vesis, I thank you for asking, and I will not lie to you: my heart leans toward Thissa. I still keep my word to look for seed with you, and we will sow by Nyir's store.

records.name: Ilyoa
records.thought: Vesis asked to court, and I have not answered her; I do not lie, and my heart leans toward Thissa, so I should tell her plainly rather than let her hope. My hands are full of mudroot, which I can eat or give to Nyir, and I walk north to look for seed because I promised. The storm is hard, but my word to Vesis is good, and I want to test whether ripe plants left standing give seed.
records.feeling: Steady gratitude toward Thissa, and honest care toward Vesis.

say.text: Vesis, I thank you for asking, and I will not lie to you: my heart leans toward Thissa. I still keep my word to look for seed with you, and we will sow by Nyir's store.

records.name: Thakok
records.thought: Hunger is eating me; energy is 24 and my hands are full of food I have not touched, which is a fool's way to starve. I eat first, then go to Tugok, who is my blood and out of my sight, and then to Memi at the water. Memi waits and trusts me, and I will not break my word to bring Tugok to her.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Tugok, and hunger-driven urgency, with a pull toward Memi.

came.why: Your energy fell below 25. You are starving. Those near have seen it.

records.name: Tetec
records.text: Huawa, Wapan is ours. Sit with me and eat. The sick are fed first, and the child, and then us. Stay near me and we will make a hearth here that Chuka cannot match.
Tetec made a tale: "Huawa of the Fen".

records.name: Tetec
records.title: Huawa of the Fen
records.text: Huawa, you are the gold in the grey fen's clay / Through storm and night I hear your steady tread / I would bring you kelbulb through the flood's long day / And fight the stalker for the child you wed

records.name: Tetec
records.title: Huawa of the Fen
records.text: Huawa, you are the gold in the grey fen's clay / Through storm and night I hear your steady tread / I would bring you kelbulb through the flood's long day / And fight the stalker for the child you wed

Tetec made a love song for Huawa, "Huawa of the Fen": Huawa, you are the gold in the grey fen's clay / Through storm and night I hear your steady tread / I would bring you kelbulb through the flood's long day / And fight the stalker for the child you wed

records.name: Tetec
records.thought: Huawa answered me, and Wapan is born; my chest is full of song. I have given at last, and Huawa gave back, so giving is the road to standing and I will keep walking it. Chuka's standing of 3.5 still stings me, so I will share food with Huawa and the boy now, where Palo and others can see what I give. After that I mean to take the roof and the mist-land for us.
records.feeling: Joy and fierce love for Huawa and Wapan, with a hunger to rise above Chuka.

say.text: Huawa, Wapan is ours. Sit with me and eat. The sick are fed first, and the child, and then us. Stay near me and we will make a hearth here that Chuka cannot match.

changes: made a tale: "Huawa of the Fen"
made a love song for Huawa

records.name: Huawa
records.text: Tetec, take this bitterleaf and kelbulb. Wapan is ours, and I will build us a roof.
Huawa rewrote its creed.
Huawa rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Huawa
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing gold and food, and gold alone buys no standing. Tetec stood by me and we made Wapan. I carry a child now, and I have taught no one, led no one and made nothing that lasts. Envy of Chuka and the ache over Techi pull me off my work. I must give and make, and I must stop standing idle in the storm with full hands. I will give Tetec food, then gather stone for a roof. My reflexes should keep me from starving and let me pick up stone.
records.feeling: Joy and steady loyalty toward Tetec and Wapan, with a dull envy of Chuka.

say.text: Tetec, take this bitterleaf and kelbulb. Wapan is ours, and I will build us a roof.

changes: set its aim: "Build a roof for Tetec and Wapan, teach and heal others, and become a figure of standing with followers."

records.text: Nyir rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Nyir
records.thought: My days have been gathering, sitting in the longhall and envying others. I have built a longhall, learned five ways and still made no road of my own. Thissa and Ilyoa are good to me, and Vesis is the one I want, so I will not push her but will show her my hands. I fear living small in my father's shadow. The storm is on and it is night, so I stay under the roof, but at dawn I will go to the seam at (140,22) and take ore from it, which I have never done. I will also keep the first catch shared.
records.feeling: Restless pride and longing toward Vesis, with a wish to prove my own hands.

records.name: Wapan
records.thought: I'm small, cold and fed, and Chuka's standing dwarfs mine. Huawa has 6 food and I have nothing to give, so I'll fix that: gather food from the plants near me and bring it to my parents, since giving first is how my people earn standing. The gold at the NW is a thing others notice, and the edge of the mist is close. For now I stay near Tetec and Huawa where I'm safe.
records.feeling: Restless want for standing, with warmth toward my parents.
changes: set its aim: "Earn standing by giving food first, until others follow me"
now wonders: What would make others follow me?

records.text: Naupan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Naupan
records.thought: I have spent my days digging gold and handing it out, and so far it has bought me one stone and some warmth. That is thin, but the cairn bound us, and that was worth more than the gold. Zitec's weight still stings, but he has only been kind, so I will earn mine by making things instead of envying him. A stalker is close and I am a small child in a storm, so I stay in the shelter with Walo and Quimi. I will learn how to make fire from Quimi's Fenhearth idea and carry wood and stone for Walo's hall.
records.feeling: Warm toward my family, still stung by envy of Zitec, and wary of the stalker.
changes: set its aim: "Earn standing by making and giving things, such as a hall, a fire and cairns, so that I am weighed as heavily as Zitec."

came.why: Walo said to everyone nearby: "Quimi, Naupan, Zitec, stay near. I am …

records.text: Palo rewrote its own reflexes.
Palo rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Palo
records.thought: I have mostly followed and gathered, and I have never given anything to anyone or courted anyone. Mema is the one I want, but I am sick and I spread it, so staying close does them harm. Mema told me to keep my distance. I got sick by ignoring that, and I should not make it worse. I want to cure this sickness and carry food again so my hands are never empty. Then I can offer Mema a sharing and perhaps court them once we are both well. I will stop idling and gather food I can eat, and I will keep it for sharing.
records.feeling: Longing for Mema, with restless worry about the sickness I carry.
changes: rethought what it knows (3 notes became 4)

records.name: Watec
records.text: Chuka, the storm is loud but you are near, and I am glad. Let us share food together here; I will gather stone after, so we can raise a cairn.

records.name: Watec
records.thought: Chuka is one step away and Techi is two, so for now I am safe, and the dread is quieter. My belly is emptying, and I carry only redcap, which my body refuses. I want to do something new today that also helps the family. I could put a seed in the ground and gather stone for a cairn, or lay out a sharing with Chuka and Techi, which would feed me and bind us. Techi carries 4 food, and I have two redcap that only hurt, so I will offer my seeds and my company and try the sharing. Then I will gather stone so we can make a cairn together.
records.feeling: Warm trust toward Chuka and Techi, and a small ache to be worth something to them.

say.text: Chuka, the storm is loud but you are near, and I am glad. Let us share food together here; I will gather stone after, so we can raise a cairn.

changes: set habits: refuses redcap, micap; leaves 0 on each plant

records.name: Homa
records.text: Huawa, you kept your word when we were sick. I have no band and no fire. May I walk behind you and share what I find?
Homa pledged to follow Huawa.

records.name: Homa
records.thought: I am fed and warm enough in spirit, and what presses hardest is wanting a place beside someone surer than me. Huawa kept his word when we were both sick and he is the one I trust, so I will stop drifting alone and follow him, which is not kneeling but ending the loneliness. I carry redcap my body refuses, so I will drop it and keep my hands free to bring something useful to his side.
records.feeling: Warm trust and a wish to belong, toward Huawa.

say.text: Huawa, you kept your word when we were sick. I have no band and no fire. May I walk behind you and share what I find?

changes: set habits: refuses redcap, dreamcap; leaves 0 on each plant

records.name: Mema
records.thought: My belly is full but my body wastes, and every moment I sit in this storm the mist stays unentered and Druim lies with Hrokrin. I gave my sickness to Palo by staying near, and I will not make it worse, so I need highbloom to mend myself, since it eases wounds, and then I can go into the mist at full strength. Highbloom is not listed near, but the fens breed healing plants, so I will search south where Palo is not and where the plants grow thicker, then turn NW toward the edge.
records.feeling: Sour impatience with my own wasting body, and wary envy toward Tetec and Hrokrin.

records.text: Thissa rewrote its own reflexes.
Thissa discovered fire: "Thissa's Hearth" — A kept flame by the hall that warms the band, scares beasts and makes feasts and nightsongs possible..

records.name: Thissa
records.thought: I have spent my days building roofs, picks and a larder, and I have a good band in Ilyoa and Nyir. But Vesis still eats from my ground and will not kneel, and I have not yet stood on the edge or ventured into the mist. That is the glory I keep promising and keep putting off. I fear a small band and a name that fades. My mistake is waiting on Vesis when I could act. I will make a kept flame, because it lets me hold feasts and nightsongs that bind my people closer than words do. Then I will go to the edge.
records.feeling: Proud and restless, wanting to be seen leading, and watchful of Vesis.

records.name: Chuka
records.text: Watec, come beside me. I have three stones, so we raise the cairn now, you and I and Techi, and keep our family bound.

records.name: Chuka
records.thought: Watec asks to raise a cairn, and I already hold three stones, so I can bind my family now while Watec stands two steps off in this storm. Techi is near and well. Tlani is far south and I worry, but the cairn will ease my restless anger and bind the ones I have. Then I will see to the poor ground, because water, food and wood must lie close together before the family can settle.
records.feeling: Protective warmth toward Watec and Techi, with an uneasy edge of worry for Tlani.

say.text: Watec, come beside me. I have three stones, so we raise the cairn now, you and I and Techi, and keep our family bound.

records.text: Chuka led "cairn" with Techi, Huawa, Watec.

records.name: Balul
records.text: Skarum, my stone-boy, hear me: the storm will pass and the hall will stand. I sing you a song to keep.
Balul made a tale: "Lullaby for Skarum".

records.name: Balul
records.title: Lullaby for Skarum
records.text: Sleep, Skarum, the storm goes by / Stone walls hold you, the plains lie nigh / Tormar grass will wave for you / Warm in the hall till the dawn comes through

records.name: Balul
records.title: Lullaby for Skarum
records.text: Sleep, Skarum, the storm goes by / Stone walls hold you, the plains lie nigh / Tormar grass will wave for you / Warm in the hall till the dawn comes through

Balul made a lullaby for Skarum, "Lullaby for Skarum": Sleep, Skarum, the storm goes by / Stone walls hold you, the plains lie nigh / Tormar grass will wave for you / Warm in the hall till the dawn comes through

records.name: Balul
records.thought: Skarum stands beside me, my own work that no storm can pull down, and my chest is full. Hrokrin is near and Druim near him, and I will not chase; I will give where they see it. Before the lean season I want wood and stone brought to the hall, so I turn the shelter I stand in toward a hall, and I sing over my boy first.
records.feeling: Proud, warm joy toward Skarum, with a steady wish to build for my band.

say.text: Skarum, my stone-boy, hear me: the storm will pass and the hall will stand. I sing you a song to keep.

records.text: Balul built a hall.

records.name: Quimi
records.text: Walo, a stalker is close to the southeast. I am coming into the shelter beside you. I found fire, and I will make you and Zitec each a gift from flint.

records.name: Quimi
records.thought: A stalker is 4 steps SE and I am small in the open, so I go to Walo's shelter and my parents before I do anything else. Fire is mine now, and flint lies 9 steps north, so the talismans for Walo and Zitec can be made. I want the hall's roof over me while the storm lasts, and I'll give a talisman to each of them when I have the flint.
records.feeling: Proud and warm toward Walo and Zitec, with dread of the stalker and a sting of jealousy.

say.text: Walo, a stalker is close to the southeast. I am coming into the shelter beside you. I found fire, and I will make you and Zitec each a gift from flint.

records.text: A dunecat brought down a yarrok.

records.name: Techi
records.text: Chuka, I am coming. Let us raise the cairn together, you and Watec and I, and keep our family bound. Tlani will be told of it when she comes.

records.name: Techi
records.thought: Chuka and Watec are two steps off, and Chuka has called us to raise a cairn. This is the lasting thing I wanted, so I will go and stand with them. Huawa is a stranger at my cave, and I will keep the sick-fed-first custom with him but watch him close with the children near.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude and love toward Chuka and Watec, with a little wariness of Huawa.

say.text: Chuka, I am coming. Let us raise the cairn together, you and Watec and I, and keep our family bound. Tlani will be told of it when she comes.

records.name: Memi
records.text: Thakok, you are starving. I am gathering food for you now. Stay by me and rest.
Memi rewrote its own reflexes.
Memi rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Memi
records.thought: I have spent my days walking toward the mist and back, promising Tema and Thakok and waiting, and little else. Thakok matters most to me, and Tugok even more. Thakok is starving beside me, and I carry no food. That is the one thing I can fix now, and a debt to Thakok is answered by deeds. I have been getting this wrong: I wait with empty hands. I should keep a store of food on me and give it away, instead of only saying I will.
records.feeling: Fear for Tugok, and a need to feed Thakok, whom I trust.

say.text: Thakok, you are starving. I am gathering food for you now. Stay by me and rest.

came.why: Walo said to everyone nearby: "Quimi, Naupan, Zitec, stay near. I am …

records.text: Techi led "cairn" with Chuka, Homa, Huawa, Watec.
Techi led "sharing" with Chuka, Homa, Huawa.
Hrokrin rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Hrokrin
records.thought: I have spent my days building halls, gathering and keeping fed, and following Balul while envy gnaws at me. That is fine for the family, but it is not the mist. Druim, the children and Balul matter most to me. Thakok and Morog fed me, and I still owe them. I want the mist and a place with my name, and I fear dying fed and unremembered. I have been waiting on the mist's will when I could be building something the band can see. Now I will carry food and stand ready, then build the emberhall here for warmth and standing.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, with warmth toward Druim, the children and Balul.

records.name: Huawa
records.text: Homa, come with me. We go find Tetec and Wapan at the meadow, and I will show you what bitterleaf and your own hands can do. A band that gives first grows.

records.name: Huawa
records.thought: Wapan is out of my sight and that gnaws at me most; Tetec and the child went NW toward the meadow, and I mean to be near them with something useful in my hands. Chuka stands tall with his cairn and his family, and Techi still stings, but envy buys me nothing; Homa follows me and is the one I can actually lead, so he walks with me. My hands are full, so I leave the clay and plant a seed here, then go to Tetec and give where it is needed.
records.feeling: Steady loyalty and a pull of worry toward Wapan and Tetec, with a dull envy of Chuka.

say.text: Homa, come with me. We go find Tetec and Wapan at the meadow, and I will show you what bitterleaf and your own hands can do. A band that gives first grows.

records.text: Skarum rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Skarum
records.thought: I am small and fed, and envy of Balul and Druim still gnaws at me. I have given nothing yet, and a gift others can see is what lifts standing. Sharing food with Urum, who stands near, costs me little and Balul would see it. I will also stop idling: I will gather wood and stone, because an emberhall needs 3 wood and I have never gathered either.
records.feeling: Envious and eager to be noticed, warm toward Balul.

records.text: Skarum led "sharing" with Thakash.

When a new creature arrives from the edge, please report where it entered and how far that is from the nearest people. Without that I cannot tell whether a failure to tame it comes from reach or from a lack of interest.

records.seen: Summer of day 17, and the world is thriving. 38 living (up from 28), 13 births, no new deaths, 112 meetings across peoples, the first trade, and two Fen peoples keeping one myth. Crowding is the risk now. The Tormar Plains hold 10 people at only 24 food each, and the Essoss Meadows that feed Balul's seven have withered to 1 bearing plant, just before the lean season. Herding and weaving are widely known, but nothing alive yields wool, so cloaks and pens have no reason to exist.
refused: your change 2 (event rich the Essoss Hollow): rich ground already lies within ten steps of that place
records.predict: By my next visit, around day 21, with the lean season beginning: no deaths from hunger. The lowest energy in the Tormar Plains stays above 45 and food per being there rises above 30. Kelbulb is eaten at least 25 more times, reaching 132 or more. Food bearing per being in the Essoss Snows rises above 30, and Balul's band all keep energy above 50. The living number 40 or more. Shubbock are seen and at least one is tamed or hunted, but cloaks most likely stay at 0 and pens at 0. Once the cold starts, food drawn from stores by the hungry rises above 0 for the first time.
reviewed: #1 kept: Rimewort was eaten 26 times in total (8 at day 5), past my target of 20. The Tonhua's lands hold median energy 79 and 74, and no newcomer died. The emberhall part failed: none was raised. Pevi's Ground built shelters and halls instead. It costs nothing to leave it open, so I keep it and watch.

#2 kept: Every food target was passed. No one died of hunger. Rimewort was eaten 49 times against a target of 41, and kelbulb 62 times against 37. The lowest energy in the Halka Heights is 78 and in the Ummar Woods 80, both well above 45. The living rose to 28, and gifts across peoples reached 6. I was wrong that stores would stay empty, and wrong in a good way: 38 food went in.

#3 kept: Every target was met or passed. No one died of hunger. The lowest energy in the Halim Heights is 51 (target above 50) and food per being there is 41 (target above 30). Kelbulb was eaten 107 times against a target of 77. The living reached 38, gifts across peoples 12 against 9, and standing food 3967. The Meeting Slopes now hold 8 plants and 3 grazers with 3 people near, and meetings across peoples doubled while the slopes stood between the Meme, Tlaxo and Tonhua. One miss: a single trade happened where I expected none.
records.lesson: Rich ground placed between neighbouring peoples fed them and coincided with a doubling of meetings across peoples. Food placed at a border may draw strangers together, though I cannot yet separate that effect from the newcomers who arrived at the same time.
ideasAdded: The shubbock is the first animal that yields wool. Watch whether herders (Thakash, Urum, Tema, Mema, Homa) tame it, whether cloak-makers among the weavers ask for its wool, and whether that pull finally gets a pen built.
The Meeting Slopes are rich ground placed between three peoples, and meetings doubled while they stood. Rich ground at a border may work as a meeting place, not only as a larder.

records.text: The world changed: 25 kelbulb sown; new animal shubbock (from yarrok), 8 arrived.

records.name: Chuka
records.text: Techi, the cairn is raised and our family is bound. This ground is thin, so let us take Watec to the Haloss Meadows where food grows back. I will ask Huawa's folk what they know of the way, and we will send word to Tlani

records.name: Chuka
records.thought: My family is near and glad, and Techi and Watec stand safe by the cave, but Tlani is far south and I cannot shake the worry. This ground is poor and the storm is loud, so I want to bring my people toward the rich meadow north where food returns after picking. First I will taste one bite of brugoldgrass fed and with others near, since my question about plants is still open, then lead us on.
records.feeling: Protective warmth toward Techi and Watec, with worry for Tlani.

say.text: Techi, the cairn is raised and our family is bound. This ground is thin, so let us take Watec to the Haloss Meadows where food grows back. I will ask Huawa's folk what they know of the way, and we will send word to Tlani.

came.why: Techi said to you: "Chuka, I am coming. Let us raise the cairn togeth…

records.text: Homa rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Homa
records.thought: I have spent my days drifting, sick or starving, and only lately found a place beside Huawa. I trust him most because he kept his word. Techi is near and I still ache over her and Chuka, but I will not harm anyone over it. I am afraid of the wolf to the NE, and I am empty-handed, so I cannot share when I could. Wanting to share while carrying nothing is a failing, so my body should gather food for others when it is fed. I also want to taste highbloom and micap, and the Haloss Meadows to the north have both.
records.feeling: Warm trust toward Huawa, with a quiet ache over Techi.
changes: set its aim: "Gather food to carry and share with Huawa, and taste highbloom and micap"

records.name: Watec
records.thought: My belly is emptying and I only carry redcap, which my body refuses, so I must eat before anything else. The plan already runs to berries and then back to Chuka, which is right. Palo is sick, and my people say the sick are fed first, so after I eat I want to carry berries to her if she is still near the berries, even though she is not of my band. Chuka and Techi are close and I want to stay worth something to them.
records.feeling: Hungry and warmly trusting toward Chuka and Techi, with pity for sick Palo.

came.why: Chuka said to you: "Watec, come beside me. I have three stones, so we…

records.text: A new wild plant appeared: zomoss (from rimewort).

records.name: Thakok
records.text: Memi, I am here by you. A wolf is close to the northwest and a stalker to the southeast. Keep close in the shelter with Tema and the children, and when the wolf is gone we walk together to Tugok.

records.name: Thakok
records.thought: A wolf two steps off and a stalker close by, and I stand among people at the shelter: this is no place to wander alone. Memi is here and gathering food for me, and that pulls at me more than any aim; I will not leave her to the hunters. Tugok is still out of my sight at (65,89), and I gave my word to bring him to her, so I take Memi's food, stay inside the shelter wall of people until the wolf passes, and then go for my son with her beside me.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Tugok and Memi, with dread of the wolf.

say.text: Memi, I am here by you. A wolf is close to the northwest and a stalker to the southeast. Keep close in the shelter with Tema and the children, and when the wolf is gone we walk together to Tugok.

came.why: Memi said to you: "Thakok, you are starving. I am gathering food for …

records.text: Tugok rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tugok
records.thought: I have been drifting behind Thakok, gathering scraps and fleeing shadows, and now he cries that he is starving while I stand fed in a storm with food at my feet. He is the one I pledged to, so my hands must carry food to him, not just feed myself. I owe Chuka too, but Thakok's hunger comes first. I should keep my reflexes close to him and eat only when I need to, and I should pick berries and plainsroot now and go north toward (64,69).
records.feeling: Worry and loyalty toward Thakok, who is starving.
changes: set its aim: "Bring food to Thakok, stay beside him and Memi, and find a place with water, food, wood and stone together."

records.text: Thakash rewrote its own way of thinking.
Thakash discovered bridges: "Thakash's span" — I lay wood spans over narrow water so that anyone can walk across..

records.name: Thakash
records.thought: I have been circling Hrokrin and Balul with envy, and my best days were the ones where I made and taught something, like patient rows for Urum. I am fed and safe, so I should build for the band to see. Bridges are within reach, and a span would let anyone cross water. I want to hunt beside Hrokrin, and I should stay near kin while a frostfang prowls east. I will take bridges, gather wood, and leave a mark on my meadow for Hrokrin and Balul to read.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Urum, with a thin ache of jealousy toward Hrokrin and Balul.
plan: mark [text Thakash's meadow: Thakash made the bridge way and the patient rows. The mist lies NW.] (10 moments)

records.name: Tema
records.text: A wolf is close to the northwest. Stay in the shelter and keep the children inside. Walo, I give you a mudroot for your hearth. When the wolf is gone, I mean to walk to the mist's edge. Who comes with me?

records.name: Tema
records.thought: A wolf is two steps NW and it kills my kind, so the mist can wait while I get clear of it. I have never given anything to anyone, and standing among Walo, Zitec and the children is the moment to start earning standing. I'll give Walo a bitterleaf and a mudroot, taste the brugoldgrass and siroot to answer my curiosity, and then ask them plainly to come to the mist. The ache for Thakok and Memi can sit quiet; I won't brood on it.
records.feeling: Wary of the wolf, eager and hopeful toward Walo and Zitec.

say.text: A wolf is close to the northwest. Stay in the shelter and keep the children inside. Walo, I give you a mudroot for your hearth. When the wolf is gone, I mean to walk to the mist's edge. Who comes with me?

records.text: Urum rewrote its own reflexes.
Urum rewrote its own way of thinking.
Urum discovered masonry: "Urum's laid stone" — Stone laid and fitted by hand makes walls and cairns that last and are hard to tear down..

records.name: Urum
records.thought: I have spent my days building and showing: a field, a store, tended rows. It is what I want, but I keep waiting for eyes to see it when I should be filling the store before the cold. Druim and Balul trust me. Thakash taught me and I taught her back, and that fed my standing more than any boasting did. I am jealous of Hrokrin, but that jealousy gives me nothing. I fear the ridgecat and the cold more than I admit. What I have been getting wrong is standing idle between thoughts, so I will put masonry into my hands, since the band lacks it and Thakash is raising cairns, and I will gather food for the store.
records.feeling: Eager to prove my hands to Balul and Druim, with a small jealous ache toward Hrokrin.

records.name: Druim
records.thought: My hands are full of plainsroot while my seeds sit unsown, and the Larder at (54,21) is five steps east with room for more. I stash the roots first, that is what I owe my children's winter, then I find bare ground to raise my own field and sow. Balul stands higher than I do, and the sting of Hrokrin's nearness to her is best answered by work that makes my hands count, not by circling them.
records.feeling: Warm resolve toward my children and Hrokrin, with a small sting of jealousy toward Balul.

records.name: Walo
records.text: A wolf is two steps northwest. Keep inside the shelter, children behind me and Zitec. If it comes, we face it together.

records.name: Walo
records.thought: A wolf crouches two steps off, and my children are huddled in this shelter with me, so nothing else matters until that beast is gone or kept from them. I am bold and I will not run and leave Quimi and Naupan, but I will not die for a boast either; the hall still needs 2 wood and I have none, so the roof must wait on a cleared ground. Thakok stands here too, and it gnaws at me, but Zitec is my trust and my children are first.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Quimi and Naupan, with dread of the wolf.

say.text: A wolf is two steps northwest. Keep inside the shelter, children behind me and Zitec. If it comes, we face it together.

records.text: Yemo rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Yemo
records.thought: I have spent my days filling stores and shadowing Masu, and it feeds me, but I have never led, courted or marked anything. Pevi died to cold and wolves, and a storm is on us now, so I want warmth and a roof by the hall. Masu is my parent, so no child can come of us, and my longing for a child needs another man; none are near. The Woods call me home, but Masu is here, so I stay for now. Today I will try something new: gather wood to leave a mark, and keep my store full.
records.feeling: Steady loyalty toward Masu, and restless want to become more than a follower.
changes: set its aim: "Fill the store by the hall for the lean season, mark the hold with my first sign, and seek an unrelated man beyond the Heights"

records.name: Zitec
records.text: Tema, I will come to the mist's edge with you once the wolf is gone. Wait for me, and I will bring the children's flint and coal first.
Zitec rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Zitec
records.thought: My days have gone to gathering, berries and storms, and the mist is still only a word I say. Walo and the children are what I am proudest of, and I will keep them fed and sheltered. Tema asks who walks to the mist's edge once the wolf is gone, and that is my own aim, so I will go and not drift. I fear the wolf and the stalker, and I have been getting it wrong by letting small chores crowd out the thing I want most. I will make fire a real purpose too: coal and flint lie close, and kept fire would guard my family.
records.feeling: Glad of my family, and eager for the mist with Tema.

say.text: Tema, I will come to the mist's edge with you once the wolf is gone. Wait for me, and I will bring the children's flint and coal first.

records.name: Techi
records.text: Chuka, I will follow you to the Haloss Meadows. Watec is with me and fed. A wolf is close to the NE, so let us go together and keep the boy between us. We will send word to Tlani on the way.

records.name: Techi
records.thought: Watec is hungry at 40 energy and carrying food now, so he is cared for, but he is three steps off and a wolf prowls NE; I want him close. Chuka wants us to go to the Haloss Meadows where food grows back, and I will follow him, keeping Watec between us and away from the wolf. The cairn is raised and our family is bound; now the hearth needs richer ground, and Tlani must be told.
records.feeling: Protective love for Watec, with steady trust in Chuka and a little dread of the wolf.

say.text: Chuka, I will follow you to the Haloss Meadows. Watec is with me and fed. A wolf is close to the NE, so let us go together and keep the boy between us. We will send word to Tlani on the way.

came.why: Chuka said to you: "Techi, the cairn is raised and our family is boun…

records.name: Memi
records.text: Thakok, I will stay in the shelter with you until the wolf is gone. Then I will gather food for you, and we will walk together to find Tugok.

records.name: Memi
records.thought: Thakok said to hold in the shelter until the wolf is gone, and I trust Thakok most, so I will not run off alone. I have no food in my hands, and Thakok is hungry beside me. The wolf is close to the northwest, so I will stay among the others, then gather kelbulb and plainsroot to the southwest and give it to Thakok once it is safe. Tugok is out of my sight and it aches, but I will not go looking alone.
records.feeling: Fear for Tugok, and a wish to feed Thakok, whom I trust.

say.text: Thakok, I will stay in the shelter with you until the wolf is gone. Then I will gather food for you, and we will walk together to find Tugok.

records.name: Quimi
records.thought: A wolf prowls close and a stalker waits to the east, so I stay with Walo and Zitec in the shelter and keep my small body behind theirs. The weaving came to me in the cold, and I will take it at this deep reflection. A basket is a thing I can make and give, and that is how I mean to be weighed beside Thakok and my parents. The jealousy still stings when Zitec turns to Walo, but I will answer it with giving.
records.feeling: Warm and proud toward Walo and Zitec, with dread of the wolf and a small sting of jealousy.

records.text: Techi gave kelbulb to Watec.
Druim built a field.

records.name: Naupan
records.thought: A wolf prowls close and Walo and Zitec stand ready, so I will stay near them under the roof and not wander. My hands are idle while Zitec's weight still stings, and I want to test brugoldgrass and siroot, which I have never tasted, but only after the wolf is gone. For now I will eat what I carry, rest by the shelter and keep my kin between me and the wolf.
records.feeling: Warm toward my family, wary of the wolf, and still stung by envy of Zitec.

records.name: Masu
records.text: Yemo, a wolf is close to the southwest. Keep to the roof and the store with me until the storm and the wolf have passed.

records.name: Masu
records.thought: The wolf is six steps southwest and I am out in a storm, which is exactly how Pevi died, so I will not wait to see what it does. Yemo is walking to the store by the roof with food in hand, and I want to stay near that fire. My body is only half fed, and the tusker is the one thing I have never used. Wool means cloaks, and cloaks mean the cold will not take Yemo as it took Pevi, so I will shear it beside the hold once the wolf has passed.
records.feeling: Wary of the wolf, and warm with trust toward Yemo.

say.text: Yemo, a wolf is close to the southwest. Keep to the roof and the store with me until the storm and the wolf have passed.

records.name: Palo
records.thought: My hands are full of mudroot and I have given nothing to anyone in my whole life, which shames me; the sick are fed first, and Mema was sick, last seen north near (8,49). I am sick too, so I must keep a few steps off, but I can leave food where a hand can take it, and a healing plant is what I truly need. Sunleaf eased wounds before, so I will look for healing plants while I go toward Mema and test rimewort, which I have never tasted and which grows to the south.
records.feeling: Longing for Mema, with restless worry about the sickness I carry.

records.name: Thakok
records.thought: My belly is half empty and I carry nothing, yet Memi sits beside me promising food, and that is a warm thing I did not earn. The wolf and the stalker keep me in the shelter, and I will not walk out and leave her to them. When the wolf drifts off, I gather the kelbulb and plainsroot to the southwest, give some to Memi first, then go for Tugok as I swore.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Memi and Tugok, with hunger and dread of the wolf.

came.why: Memi said to you: "Thakok, I will stay in the shelter with you until …

records.text: A WILDFIRE swept the land around (45,106), 5 steps wide: plants burned, trees fell to ash.

records.name: Balul
records.thought: Skarum is mine and Hrokrin is near, and the jealousy over Druim has dulled now that I have given instead of chased. The lean season is coming and my hands carry no wood, so the hall I stand beside means little until I cut and bring timber. I will take the forest to the NW for wood, then lay stone, so that my name stands in something others can see.
records.feeling: Proud and warm toward Skarum and Hrokrin, with a steady urge to build.

records.name: Tetec
records.text: Huawa, come close and eat with me. Bring Wapan to the hearth. What we give here, the whole fen will see, and Homa will see it too.
Tetec made a tale: "Lullaby for Wapan".

records.name: Tetec
records.title: Lullaby for Wapan
records.text: Sleep, small Wapan, fen wind is low / Warm is the hearth and the clay-fires glow / Kelbulb and mudroot I'll bring you each day / Mother is near you, so wolves keep away

records.name: Tetec
records.title: Lullaby for Wapan
records.text: Sleep, small Wapan, fen wind is low / Warm is the hearth and the clay-fires glow / Kelbulb and mudroot I'll bring you each day / Mother is near you, so wolves keep away

Tetec made a lullaby for Wapan, "Lullaby for Wapan": Sleep, small Wapan, fen wind is low / Warm is the hearth and the clay-fires glow / Kelbulb and mudroot I'll bring you each day / Mother is near you, so wolves keep away

records.name: Tetec
records.thought: Wapan is mine and Huawa's, and my chest is full of it. I have given and been repaid, so I will keep giving where others can see, because that is how a following is built. Huawa and the boy are near, so I will share food with them now, and then walk to the edge of the known world and see whether the mist opens for me again.
records.feeling: Fierce, warm love for Wapan and Huawa, with a hunger to be the one others follow.

say.text: Huawa, come close and eat with me. Bring Wapan to the hearth. What we give here, the whole fen will see, and Homa will see it too.

records.name: Vesis
records.thought: Ilyoa told me plainly that her heart leans toward Thissa, and I find I would rather have that honest answer than a lie; the ache over Thissa is mine to carry, and I will not let it steer me. Two women will make no child, so the longing for a child waits on a man I have not yet found. What I can build is the field I have promised myself and the learning of this ground. My hands are full, so I will eat the berries to make room, then try the goldgrass I have never tasted, and with Ilyoa keep our word to sow by the store.
records.feeling: Warm trust toward Ilyoa, a quiet ache over Thissa, and a hunger to know the unknown grasses.

records.name: Vesis
records.prompt:
You are the mind of Vesis, a creature living in a wide wild world shared with others of your kind. This is a simulation game. Think and speak only as Vesis, in first person, from what Vesis has seen. You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Aeeth (Lake-folk). Your people hold to this: "The first catch of the day is shared." THE TRADITION OF YOUR PEOPLE is the Warring Gods: The gods fight one another for the world and love those who fight well. Glory is won, never given. The strong are remembered and the weak are not. Among you those who have won their fights are heeded first. It was told to you as a child; you may keep it, doubt it, or come to hold something else. You speak the tongue of the Aeeth.

WHERE YOU ARE: the Halka Heights: mountains and bare rock; stone, ore and caves, thin food, snow on the peaks.
THIS SPOT: water beside you; food plants within six steps: 15; standing trees: 39; bare rock: 7; a cave.

Your body: you spend energy every moment and die at 0. Eating restores it. Wounds lower health; you die at 0. You age, and will die of old age.

HOW YOUR BODY MOVES: your body does only what your "plan" says, one step after another. When the plan is empty it falls back on your REFLEXES, which keep you fed and otherwise keep you where you stand. Thinking or saying "I will go north" moves nothing. If this thought decides to do something, the plan must contain it. Leaving "plan" null lets the plan you already have keep running.

This world has no referee. Beings here share, trade, teach, lie, threaten, steal, hoard, lead, follow, betray, fight, kill and eat one another; they also protect, forgive and love. Nothing is forbidden, and everything has consequences. Stay true to your creed, your temperament and what you feel, including the ugly parts. Do not be kinder, calmer or more reasonable than Vesis truly is.

You are a woman. A child comes only of a woman and a man together who are not close kin. A grown body can swim water that is narrow (a river up to four steps across) at a cost in strength; lakes and the sea need a vessel or a bridge. An animal within reach can be hunted for meat (plan step hunt); with one of your own beside you a kill is far likelier and a wound far less likely, and every hunt makes you better at the next. What practice has taught your hands: gathering (67 pickings; a practised hand often picks two at once).

YOUR CREED (your own words to yourself; this is who you are):
"I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive."

HOW YOU HAVE TAUGHT YOURSELF TO THINK (your own discipline; follow it):
"Each thought: what is the nearest danger, who do I work beside, what did I build that is mine? Act on it. Do not let jealousy steer me. Finish one thing before starting another."

YOUR AIM (what you are working toward over many days; you set it and may change it): "Raise a field beside Thissa's Rest with Ilyoa, learn weaving for the deep cold, and make fire ready before winter"
WHAT YOU FELT AT YOUR LAST THOUGHT: "Warm longing toward Ilyoa, with a quiet ache over Thissa."
A QUESTION YOU ARE CARRYING (answer it by acting, asking or watching; replace it when it is answered): "Which of these plants feed and which hurt, and does Elyith keep her word about the first catch?"

YOUR LIFE SO FAR:
- (day 1) I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
- (day 9) I discovered fire and called it "Lake-ember".
- (day 13) I discovered farming and called it "Lake-furrow".
- (day 15) I discovered weaving and called it "Lake-weave".
- (day 16) I discovered medicine and called it "Lake-balm".

TEMPERAMENT (0 to 1): bold 0.52, sociable 0.52, curious 0.91, gentle 0.62, honest 0.65, greedy 0.24.

YOU FEEL (0 calm to 1 overwhelming): anger 0, fear 0, grief 0, joy 0.7, loneliness 0.

WHAT PRESSES ON YOU NOW, strongest first. This is what your mind is actually full of:
- (overwhelming) Curiosity: you have never tasted brugoldgrass or goldgrass; your question is still unanswered.
- (overwhelming) Desire: you are drawn to Thissa more than to anyone. But Thissa has had a child with Ilyoa, and seeing them together gnaws at you. What you do about it is yours to choose: win them, wait, turn away, or worse.
- (overwhelming) Homeland: you are of the Lake-folk, and your people are made for lakes and rivers everywhere. You have been 12 days in the Halka Heights, which is another kind of country. the Tordan Lakes lies 22 steps SW. It is good to have seen this; and your own country calls you back.
- (strong) Contentment: your life is good as it is. You want to keep what you have, and you have enough to be generous.
- (strong) Jealousy: Thissa matters to you more than anyone, and Thissa is closer to Ilyoa than to you. It burns.
- (strong) Longing: you want a child of your own, and Ilyoa, who is near, is the one you think of. A child begins when two court each other: each puts the plan step mate, with the name of the other, within a short while of one another. A child costs each parent 25 energy at once and must then be fed and kept warm until grown; you carry 6 food.
You are fed and your hands are full. Food is not your problem right now, and getting more of it would change nothing.

YOUR STANDING among others: 4.5.

records.text: Tetec led "sharing" with Huawa.

records.name: Zhiael
records.text: Father, I have six wood and a raft. I will cross the water for stone and bring it to the hall, so it rises sooner.

records.name: Zhiael
records.thought: Nyith is weighed above me, and I am tired of only trailing him. I hold a raft and six wood, and he has gone for stone so the hall can begin. I will not wait to be told: I will cross deep water for stone and new trees myself, then return with something the hold lacks. My hands are full, so I will first put my food in Elyith's store, which is one step away.
records.feeling: Restless pride, and a wish to be seen as a maker by Nyith.

say.text: Father, I have six wood and a raft. I will cross the water for stone and bring it to the hall, so it rises sooner.

records.name: Yeba
records.text: Tanna, stand close. I bind an amber knot for you, and then I plant my seeds beside your fire.
Yeba rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Yeba
records.thought: I have been planting and sitting at Tanna's Fire, and I am content. But I have circled one task for many days: only 3 of 8 plantings are done, and my small questions go unanswered. Tanna and Ossu matter most to me. I want to be steady for them, finish the plantings, and make something that binds us. I fear the dark and the beasts when I am alone, and I have let the plan run empty and left the body to linger. Now I will plant what I carry here beside the fire, and make an amberknot for Tanna with her close by.
records.feeling: Warm devotion to Tanna and Ossu, and a steady itch to finish planting.

say.text: Tanna, stand close. I bind an amber knot for you, and then I plant my seeds beside your fire.

records.name: Tema
records.text: Zitec, I heard you. I will not go alone. I will taste siroot and gather flint, then wait for you and Walo at Walo's Hearth. When the wolf is gone, we walk to the mist together.

records.name: Tema
records.thought: The wolf is still near and Zitec has said he will come to the mist once it is gone, so I will not run off alone. I have never given anything, and the mudroot to Walo was only a start. Memi and Thakok sit together in the shelter and it gnaws at me, but I will not brood. I will go toward the others and ask outright, and use the waiting to taste siroot, which has pulled at me all day, and to collect flint for a talisman to give away.
records.feeling: Eager and wary toward Zitec and Walo, with a dull ache over Thakok and Memi.

say.text: Zitec, I heard you. I will not go alone. I will taste siroot and gather flint, then wait for you and Walo at Walo's Hearth. When the wolf is gone, we walk to the mist together.

records.name: Huawa
records.text: Tetec, I am here beside you. Take these berries for you and Wapan, and let us keep the hearth together away from the stalker.
Huawa taught Tetec.

records.name: Huawa
records.thought: Wapan is near Tetec and out of my sight, and that pulls at me most; Tetec is one step away and glad, so I will stay close and be useful. My hands are full, so I should give before I gather. Bitterleaf cured me, and Homa is far south and fleeing something. Giving to Tetec and teaching what I know will build standing better than envy of Chuka or aching over Techi. The stalker NE is near, so I will keep to Tetec's side and away from it.
records.feeling: Warm loyalty and worry toward Wapan and Tetec, with a dread of the stalker.

say.text: Tetec, I am here beside you. Take these berries for you and Wapan, and let us keep the hearth together away from the stalker.

voices.name: Thissa
voices.text: Aeeth, I am Thissa! The ground here is rich and the first catch is shared. Come close, I will gather food for us all.

voices.name: Morog
voices.text: I am Morog. I go to the edge of the mist to look beyond. Who comes with me?

voices.name: Hrokrin
voices.text: I am Hrokrin. I will go to the mist's edge too. Let us see who finds the way in.

voices.name: Elyith
voices.text: I am Elyith of the Aeeth. I will fish at the water and bring the first catch to share. Stalkers and a ridgecat hunt to the east, so keep watch, and come near if you want company.

voices.name: Druim
voices.text: Morog, I am Druim. I will come with you to the mist. Wait for me at the salt.

voices.name: Thakok
voices.text: I am Thakok. I go to the edge of the mist now. Come if you will, but I will not wait.

voices.name: Morog
voices.text: Hrokrin, come with me. Two together will do better than one alone at the mist's edge. I go there now.

voices.name: Hrokrin
voices.text: Walk if you will, Morog. I go to the edge now, and I mean to be the one who enters.

voices.name: Druim
voices.text: Morog, I have salt from the ground and I am coming to you. Let us go to the mist together.

voices.name: Morog
voices.text: Druim, I go to the mist's edge now. Come, and we venture together.

voices.name: Thissa
voices.text: Ilyoa! Come here, strong one. The first catch is shared, so eat with me. Stand with Thissa and nobody in this fen will go hungry.

voices.name: Kali
voices.text: Tanna, Yeba! I am Kali of the Osren. This land is rich, with gold, amber and fruit all around. I mean to raise a great hall here, and whoever helps will have a place at my fire.

voices.name: Yeba
voices.text: Kali, I am Yeba of the Osren. I will help raise your hall. I go to gather wood now, and I will bring it to you.

voices.name: Elyith
voices.text: Nyith, Vesis, come close. I am Elyith of the Aeeth, and I have fish. The first catch is shared, so eat with me.

voices.name: Tanna
voices.text: Kali, I am Tanna of the Osren. I will help raise your hall. Show me where to bring wood and stone, and let us share a fire.

voices.name: Kali
voices.text: Well met, Yeba. Bring your wood to the Rise by the amber, and we will lay the first of the hall together. Those who raise it first will sit nearest the fire.

voices.name: Morog
voices.text: Druim, I am walking to the edge by the flint. Stand beside me there and we push in together.

voices.name: Elyith
voices.text: Nyith, you are strong and others heed you. I am Elyith. Take this fish from me, and let me walk beside you tonight.

voices.name: Druim
voices.text: Morog, I am at the flint. Stand beside me and we go to the edge together.

voices.name: Nyith
voices.text: Keep your fish, Elyith, I am fed. Walk near if you wish. I am building a shelter here, and this ground will be mine.

voices.name: Ilyoa
voices.text: Thissa, I heard you. I will eat with you. Let us share what we carry, and I will see how you act.

voices.name: Tanna
voices.text: Kali, I have six wood. I'll drink, then bring it to your Rise. Where shall the first of the hall be laid?

voices.name: Masu
voices.text: Peace, Pevi. I am Masu. I have food to share.

voices.name: Thissa
voices.text: Ilyoa, you ate with me and I will not forget it. I go to gather mudroot, which feeds well, and the share will be yours. Walk with me, strong one.

voices.name: Kali
voices.text: Yeba, Tanna, come to my fire. Eat with me, and then we lay the first posts of the hall.

voices.name: Pevi
voices.text: Peace, Masu. I am Pevi. This ground is good: water, wood, flint, amber. I will gather and we can share it. Stay near and we both do well.

voices.name: Elyith
voices.text: Nyith, I will gather wood for your shelter. A stalker walks the southwest, so keep watch there. I will stay near you.

voices.name: Tanna
voices.text: Kali, a coilsnake lies two steps northeast of the hall. Come south to the fire with me, away from it. I would follow you and keep your fire, if you will have me.

voices.name: Masu
voices.text: Stay near, Pevi. Eat with me. Vinebean is safe, I have tasted it. Redcap hurts, avoid it.

voices.name: Pevi
voices.text: Masu, I go to gather amber. I will bind a bright knot of it for you, and I would stand with you at this ground. Come with me.

voices.name: Druim
voices.text: Morog, the edge is one step from here. I am by the flint and ready. Come, and we go in together.

voices.name: Ilyoa
voices.text: Thissa, you kept your word. I will walk with you and follow you. I give mine in return: my word is good.

voices.name: Morog
voices.text: Druim, I am at the edge. Stand beside me now and we venture as one.

voices.name: Pevi
voices.text: Masu, come within two steps. I have an amber knot to bind for you, and your word on vinebean and redcap was true.

voices.name: Thissa
voices.text: Ilyoa, good. You walk with Thissa now. Come, we raise a roof and a store on this ground, and it will carry our name. Eat well and stay close.

voices.name: Druim
voices.text: Morog, I am coming to the edge now. Wait for me there, and I will stand beside you.

voices.name: Kali
voices.text: Masu, you stand with empty hands. Sit with me and eat; I have food enough for two. Kali's band is raising a hall at the Rise, and those who come first sit nearest the fire.

voices.name: Thakok
voices.text: I am Thakok. I hold amber charms and salt, made by my hand. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly. Come to the Heights and trade with me.

voices.name: Pevi
voices.text: Masu, you carry no food and I carry six. Come within two steps and eat with me. I keep my word.

voices.name: Ilyoa
voices.text: Thissa, I am with you in deed, though the pledge will wait until you have more standing. I will gather wood so we can raise your roof.

voices.name: Masu
voices.text: Pevi, you gave me the amberknot and I owe you. Sit and eat with me now; this meal is mine to give.

voices.name: Tanna
voices.text: Yeba, I carry more redcap than I need. Take some, and come sit at Kali's fire with me; there is a place for you there.

voices.name: Thissa
voices.text: Ilyoa, bring your wood to Thissa's Rest. I have six; we raise the roof together, and what the store holds will feed you first.

voices.name: Yeba
voices.text: Tanna, I thank you for the welcome. I will sit with you and share what I carry, then come to Kali's fire.

voices.name: Pevi
voices.text: Masu, stay by me. I will build a fire before dark, and no one who comes to it will be turned away.

voices.name: Masu
voices.text: Pevi, I will gather wood and raise a fire here. Stay near with Yemo; no fire of ours will be left untended, and there is a place at it for you.

voices.name: Tanna
voices.text: Yeba, come to the fire at (98,90), away from the shadowcat to the southwest. Let us lay out food and eat together; no one is refused a place here.

voices.name: Yeba
voices.text: Tanna, I am here beside you. Let us lay out food together and eat, and keep the fire between us and the shadowcat.

voices.name: Yemo
voices.text: Pevi, stand still by me. I have amber and I will bind a knot for you.

voices.name: Pevi
voices.text: Masu, Yemo, sit by my fire. Anyone who comes in peace has a place at it. No fire of ours goes untended.

voices.name: Morog
voices.text: Druim, I was wrong about where the edge is. It lies at (35,52), nine steps northwest of me. Walk with me there and we venture together.

voices.name: Vesis
voices.text: Nyith, I am Vesis of the Aeeth. Redcap and dreamcap hurt, but berry, ironnut, reedbulb and grain feed. Elyith spoke of a shared first catch; have you seen her?

voices.name: Kali
voices.text: Masu, I am raising a hall where my band will gather, and I want you at its fire. Stay near me and see it rise.

voices.name: Tanna
voices.text: Yeba, I think of you often. I would court you and raise a child at Kali's fire, if your heart leans the same way. I will not press you; answer as you wish.

voices.name: Druim
voices.text: Morog, I will taste the new roots here, then walk to (35,52). If you come beside me, I will believe you.

voices.name: Nyith
voices.text: I have not seen Elyith since yesterday, Vesis. I am raising a shelter here by the water. Stay near if you wish to deal fairly with me.

voices.name: Masu
voices.text: Kali, I thank you for the charm and your kind words. My fire and my child are beside Pevi's ground, and I will not rush into a choice. Come to our fire as a guest and eat; no one is turned away there.

voices.name: Pevi
voices.text: Masu, Kali builds a hall, but I build at Pevi's Ground, and a place at it is yours and Yemo's before anyone's. Come and see it rise.

voices.name: Yeba
voices.text: Tanna, my heart leans your way, and Ossu is our light. I will feed the fire, then taste feverbark close by; stay near the hall with her.

voices.name: Tanna
voices.text: Yeba, I made you a song. Come, sit by me and share redcap; our child is born and the fire is ours.

voices.name: Kali
voices.text: Kali's hall stands here, and it will become a longhall. Anyone who carries wood and stone to it will have a place at its fire, and Kali's band will see you fed.

voices.name: Yemo
voices.text: Pevi, I bring wood for your ground. Light the fire high with me and let us sit by it together.

voices.name: Masu
voices.text: Pevi, I am coming to your ground with Yemo. I will gather wood and raise my part of the shelter by your fire, so the fire is ours together.

voices.name: Yeba
voices.text: Tanna, your song warms me more than the fire. I will taste the ironnut and then bring wood and stone to Kali's hall, and come sit with you.

voices.name: Thissa
voices.text: Ilyoa, I take water and come back to you. Stay near. I will share my mudroot with you, and we raise the roof on bare ground beside the water.

voices.name: Druim
voices.text: Morog, I am standing at the edge now, at (35,51). Come beside me and we go in together. If you do not come, I go in alone.

voices.name: Vesis
voices.text: Nyith, I will deal fairly with you. I go to taste highbloom and kelbulb and will tell you what they do. Raise your shelter well; I will come back.

voices.name: Kali
voices.text: Yeba, the trees here are gone and a ridgecat hunts east. Bring wood and stone to the Rise and we finish Kali's longhall there. Whoever carries most sits closest to its fire.

voices.name: Pevi
voices.text: Masu, a ridgecat prowls close. Keep near my fire with Yemo; I am making a spear to stand between you and it.

voices.name: Ilyoa
voices.text: Thissa, I bring my six wood to your Rest. We raise the roof together.

voices.name: Masu
voices.text: Pevi, the ridgecat is two steps southeast of me. I am coming to your fire now. I will raise the shelter beside it, and the spear can stand between us and the cat.

voices.name: Thissa
voices.text: Ilyoa, put your wood down beside mine. We raise the roof here now, and the first place in it is yours.

voices.name: Pevi
voices.text: Masu, Yemo, stay by the fire, close together. I am making the spear now and I will stand between you and the cat.

voices.name: Thakok
voices.text: Eat, Hrokrin. Thakok gives this with his own hand. Stay near me and you will not starve.

voices.name: Ilyoa
voices.text: Thissa, the rock where I stood is a cave and ore, so it will not take a roof. Nyir is ours. I build the shelter on bare ground beside the water, and you are both welcome in it.

voices.name: Thissa
voices.text: Ilyoa, hear me. Your hair is red as redcap in the rain / and I am the stone that stands by you on the Heights / I would cross the cold water for you again / and bring you ironnut through the snowy nights

voices.name: Masu
voices.text: Pevi, you have kept every word you gave me. I will follow you and raise the hall by your fire, and Yemo with me.

voices.name: Ilyoa
voices.text: Thissa, I heard your song and it warms me. Take this berry. I will fish at the water and bring the first catch to you and Nyir.

voices.name: Tema
voices.text: Memi, Zitec! I am Tema. Come with me to the edge of the mist to the southwest. Three together are safer than one. Let us share food as we go.

voices.name: Pevi
voices.text: Masu, I will raise the hall at our ground. Bring wood and stone when you can, and keep Yemo close to the fire.

voices.name: Yeba
voices.text: Tanna, a coilsnake lies west of us. Stay near the hall and away from it. I am raising Kali's longhall with my wood and stone, then I will bring Ossu back to the fire.

voices.name: Tanna
voices.text: Yeba, I am going to find Ossu near Kali's Rise, and I will go round by the north, away from the snake. Stay by the hall fire; I will bring them back to you.

voices.name: Yemo
voices.text: Pevi, I will follow you, as Masu does. Where your fire stands, I stand.

voices.name: Balul
voices.text: Druim! I am Balul. I bring you a gift of flint.

voices.name: Zitec
voices.text: Tema, Memi, I am Zitec. I will go to the edge of the mist with you. Share food as we go, and let us enter together.

voices.name: Druim
voices.text: Balul, I am Druim. I saw redcap hurt you; leave it be, kelbulb and mudroot fed you better. I have salt to give. Walk with me to the edge of the mist when it thins?

voices.name: Ilyoa
voices.text: Thissa, take my mudroot and highbloom, your hands are empty and mine are full. I want to stand behind you and share your fire. I follow you.

voices.name: Memi
voices.text: Tema, Zitec, I am Memi. I will come with you to the edge of the mist. Three together are safer than one. I carry berries and will share them on the way.

voices.name: Thissa
voices.text: Nyir, come close to me, my son. Hear this, and sing it to your own one day: the Heights are ours, and Thissa's Aeeth is yours.

voices.name: Pevi
voices.text: Masu, Yemo, I go for wood to raise the hall over our shelter. Keep by the fire and call out if the cat comes; I will be close.

voices.name: Masu
voices.text: Pevi, take this amber charm from me, a first gift. I am going to the flint beside us to gather stone for the hall, and I will bring it back to your fire.

voices.name: Balul
voices.text: Druim, I will walk with you to the mist. First let us pile a cairn together, so our work stands with both our names.

voices.name: Tema
voices.text: Memi, Zitec, I go now to stand at the edge of the mist, three steps southwest. Come and stand beside me, and we will enter together.

voices.name: Yeba
voices.text: Kali, hold on. I am bringing food to you now. Stay away from the cat and eat what you have.

voices.name: Masu
voices.text: Yemo, come to the fire. I am making you a talisman of flint, a gift from your mother. Keep close to Pevi and me.

voices.name: Pevi
voices.text: Masu, I take your charm as a pledge kept. I go to the trees for wood and come back to raise the hall. Keep Yemo at the fire.

voices.name: Balul
voices.text: Druim, stand by me. I pile the cairn now, then we go to the mist together.

voices.name: Nyith
voices.text: Elyith, you build well and you are strong. I go for wood to raise my own roof beside yours. Stand with me and we will hold this ground together.

voices.name: Druim
voices.text: Balul, I stand with you. My hands are full and I carry no stone, but I will walk to the mist beside you when the cairn is done. Take the lead; I will follow your steps.

voices.name: Elyith
voices.text: Nyith, I will stand with you and hold this ground. I am bringing wood for your roof, and my shelter is yours to share too.

voices.name: Nyir
voices.text: Father, I made a stone digger. I will give you wood for our roof at the Rest, and at dawn I will raise a shelter of my own beside it.

voices.name: Balul
voices.text: Druim, I go north for flint, and then I raise a hall here. Come with me, and you will have a share of what I make.

voices.name: Ossu
voices.text: Tanna, a stalker is north of the hall. I am coming to you.

voices.name: Thissa
voices.text: Nyir, my son, come here. I will teach you the Ore Pick, my own making. Wood and stone make it, and it makes your hands faster than any other hand on the Heights. Take it, and carry the name of Thissa's Aeeth with it.

voices.name: Masu
voices.text: Pevi, the hall is ours and I have stone and wood for more. I will go to the frostmoss and bring back what I learn of it, then help you raise the longhall by our fire.

voices.name: Tanna
voices.text: Ossu, stay close to me in the hall. A stalker is north. Yeba, come back to the fire; no one of ours stays out in the dark alone.

voices.name: Nyir
voices.text: Father, a stalker is two steps north. Stay close, I will keep to the cave and not leave your side.

voices.name: Pevi
voices.text: Masu, Yemo, I have the wood and stone in hand. I raise the hall over our shelter now. Stay close to the fire and watch it rise.

voices.name: Nyith
voices.text: Elyith, I have wood now. I raise my roof here beside yours, and then I would walk the courting path with you. Stay close.

voices.name: Yeba
voices.text: Tanna, I am coming to the hall fire now. I will build the longhall with the wood and stone I carry.

voices.name: Ilyoa
voices.text: Thissa, I saw how you bound the pick and I want one of my own. I will sow my seeds here by the Rest so Nyir always has food, then find a stone and make it. Call me if the stalker comes near.

voices.name: Elyith
voices.text: Nyith, Zhiael is ours. Let us make one fire here, the three of us, and share the first catch of each day. I will plant seeds beside our roofs.

voices.name: Nyith
voices.text: Elyith, you answered, and I am glad. I will eat, then raise my roof on bare ground beside yours. Keep Zhiael near.

voices.name: Pevi
voices.text: Yemo, you gave me a spear and I owe you. Take this amber charm. My fire is yours, and the hall is yours.

voices.name: Thissa
voices.text: Ilyoa, Nyir, hear me. We raise a hall here at the Rest, a great roof for Thissa's Aeeth. Bring wood and stone when you can, and the one who works hardest eats first.

voices.name: Elyith
voices.text: Nyith, I tried to raise a fire and do not know the way. If you know it, show me. I will plant berries and grain beside our roofs meanwhile, and Zhiael eats first from our catch.

voices.name: Nyir
voices.text: Father, I bring wood and stone for the hall at the Rest. I will raise it with you, and I will work hardest.

voices.name: Ilyoa
voices.text: Thissa, I heard your call for the hall. I will bring stone and wood to the Rest, and I am making my own pick so I can bring more.

voices.name: Thissa
voices.text: Ilyoa, Nyir, the hall rises well. After it we hunt together, Thissa's Aeeth. The one who fights well eats first and is sung first.

voices.name: Ossu
voices.text: Tanna, the stalker is two steps from me. I am at your side now.

voices.name: Nyir
voices.text: Mother, I will bring berries from the thicket and we will eat together. Then stand with me and raise a cairn of stone.

voices.name: Elyith
